claims.claim: A PR fingerprint is {kind, repository, number, base_sha, head_sha} built from --expect-head and --expect-base full OIDs; a plan fingerprint is {kind, sha256, bytes} built from --expect-sha256. The printed fingerprint is the SHA-256 of that canonical JSON.

claims.correction: A PR revision is {kind, repository, number, base_sha, head_sha}. The main supplies only head_sha and base_sha, as full 40- or 64-hex OIDs through --expect-head and --expect-base. repository and number are copied from the captured PR (revision.py:42-54). A plan revision is {kind, sha256, bytes}. The main supplies only sha256 through --expect-sha256, and bytes is taken from the captured file (revision.py:55-60). The fingerprint is the SHA-256 of the sorted, compact JSON of that revision (revision.py:83-86). It is printed only by the dry-run preview (service.py:109-114).

claims.claim: The captured artifact must equal the main's expected revision when a round is reserved and again when the peer's output is consumed; a change blocks the round with exit 4.
A PR gate requires the local checkout to be at the exact PR head with a clean worktree (untracked files included), checked at capture and before merge.
`--peer` accepts fable, astra or sol; sol is remapped to astra with a stderr notice, and the service refuses any other peer, so there is no Opus peer.

Both the shipped default policy and the live override define models.fable as claude-fable-5-1 (provider claude) and models.astra as gpt-6-astra with effort ultra, so `--peer fable` is still accepted by the live daemon.

Each round is submitted as SubmitArgs kind gate-review with sandbox read-only, pinned_model = peer, pinned_lane = --peer-account, max_attempts 1, isolated_review True, review_root, round_lease gate:<id>:round:<n>, and request_id gate:<id>:round:<n>:<token>; the gate CLI never parents a provider process.
The daemon refuses a gate-review job without a pinned model, without isolated_review, without a gate:<id>:round:<n> lease, or whose cwd is not a non-repository directory under the state root.

The review root is the caller's PR checkout for a PR gate and the neutral round directory for a plan gate; the neutral directory is <state root>/reviews/<gate id>/<NNN>-<token> and is refused if it falls inside the repository.

An isolated Claude peer runs in plan mode with a fixed tool list that drops web access, `--setting-sources ""`, `--safe-mode`, no Chrome, an empty strict MCP config, no slash commands, and `--add-dir <review root>`; memory environment variables are removed.

An isolated Codex peer is launched with --ephemeral, --ignore-user-config, --ignore-rules and hooks, plugins, memories, multi-agent, browser and web search disabled, after inspecting its config layers and MCP inventory; managed requirements are refused. The review root is not added to the Codex argv.
Inherited CLAUDE_CODE_MANAGED_SETTINGS_PATH, CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SETTINGS_PATH or CLAUDE_CODE_MOCK_REMOTE_SETTINGS refuses a gate (exit 4) and an isolated run.
Main and peer model families are compared only when `--main-model` is passed; otherwise main_family is set to the complement of the peer's provider without any observation.
Nothing compares the peer's lane account with the main's account. `--peer-account` and `--exclude-account` are accepted only for a fable peer, and the gate submission carries no caller_session.
claims.evidence: subfleet/gate/service.py:47-56; subfleet/gate/round.py:60-72 (no caller_session field set); grep of subfleet/gate/*.py for caller|session|account finds only routing

claims.claim: A gate round never sets allow_desktop, so the scheduler excludes a lane flagged as the desktop app's own account, as it does for every job without allow_desktop.
The independent=True flag on the gate submission only exempts a job from a cancelled parent's refusal and kill tree; it is not an identity check.

Verdict parsing fails closed: exactly one begin and end sentinel, no text outside them, no duplicate JSON keys or NaN/Infinity, schema_version 1, artifact_revision equal to the expected revision, verdict in {approve, changes_requested, blocked}, findings with nonempty severity/location/description, approve with empty findings and notes, changes_requested with at least one finding. Every failure is exit 4.
The peer job must have succeeded with rc 0, its accepted attempt must have requested the policy model id for the peer, and the deliverable's bytes must still match the SHA-256 recorded at acceptance.

Attestation rules: a Claude (claude-*) peer round must be positively attested with a served model equal to, or prefixed by, the requested id; a Codex round counts when unattested; a mismatch or any downgrade record (file marker or evidence key) discards the round for either provider.
An isolated --ephemeral Codex run yields UNATTESTED when no unique persisted rollout with model evidence is found.
An attestation failure automatically reserves a new round, which counts against the round cap.
The round limit is min(--max-rounds, caps.gate_max_rounds), and 0 or no value means the cap; gate_max_rounds is 4 in both the shipped default and the live override.
After changes_requested, continuing on an unchanged artifact without --response is refused with exit 3.
The round lease key gate:<id>:round:<n> is taken at admission with holder gate-round:<job id>; a second round for the same gate is refused while another holder or a live round exists.

The round lease has no time-based expiry: it is deleted only when the gate consumes the finished round, and output whose lease was lost is discarded. Job-end lease deletions match holder = job or attempt id, never gate-round:<job id>.

claims.claim: The gate does not set max_wall_s, so a peer job gets the policy cap (21600 s) and is killed when a started job reaches it.

The gate CLI polls every 0.25 s until the daemon returns an exit code, with no overall deadline; only a daemon that answers busy is retried for up to 180 s per poll. An interrupt leaves the peer job in the store.

Read surfaces are `gate continue <id> --dry-run` (reads gate.json and recaptures the subject without a daemon), the gate.json and certificate.json projections under <state root>/gates/<id>/, and `subfleet runs --kind gate-review` for peer jobs. There is no gate-level abort; killing the peer job makes the next poll record the round blocked.
Gate state is journaled as gate.state events in SQLite, and the newest event wins over the file projection.
A merge requires a PR gate with --on-agreement merge, a latest round approved by the peer with empty findings and notes, and a main approval of the same revision.

Before merging, the PR must be OPEN, not a draft, at the approved head and base, MERGEABLE, mergeStateStatus CLEAN, with a nonempty set of checks all terminal and green; the command is `gh pr merge <n> --repo <r> --match-head-commit <head> --merge|--squash`, run once with a 30 s timeout and never retried.

Each merge is a durable action keyed by repository:number:head with a fenced holder; an ambiguous outcome is settled by later reads, never by a second submission, and a landing is confirmed only when the merge commit's parents are [base] (squash) or [base, head] (merge).
Gate exit codes: 0 agreement or completion, 1 operational error, 2 invalid input, 3 changes requested, 4 blocked or invalid review, 5 failed, unverified or queued merge action.

additions.name: Daemon-journaled gate state
additions.description: Gate state is a sequence of gate.state events in the SQLite store; gate.json and certificate.json are projections, and the CLI is a poller of gate.start/gate.poll/gate.continue. A daemon restart reads the journal and does not re-dispatch.

additions.name: Policy round cap
additions.description: caps.gate_max_rounds (4 in the default and live policy) bounds every gate; --max-rounds can only lower it.

additions.name: Round lease and neutral review directory
additions.description: Each round holds gate:<id>:round:<n> from admission until the gate consumes it, runs from <state root>/reviews/<gate>/<round> outside any repository, and output from a lost lease is discarded.

additions.name: Isolated peer environment
additions.description: Claude peers run plan-mode with no settings sources, MCP, Chrome, web or memory; Codex peers run --ephemeral with user config, rules, hooks, plugins, memories and web search disabled after a config-layer and MCP inspection that refuses managed requirements.

additions.name: Durable, fenced merge actions
additions.description: A merge is an actions row keyed by repository:number:head with a holder fence; one remote call with --match-head-commit, ambiguity settled by reads, landing verified by merge-commit parents, and queue or auto-merge detected.

additions.name: Explicit family check
additions.description: `--main-model` makes the gate refuse a peer of the same provider family; without it the family is inferred.

additions.name: Layered API-key refusal
additions.description: API-key Codex homes are refused at enrollment, on a pinned submit, before probes and launches, and by the _api-lane-check verb the PATH shim calls; API-key variables are stripped from the daemon and every child.

additions.name: Verified Codex never-rules preflight
additions.description: Each non-isolated Codex launch verifies the operator's private hook overlay against TRUST pins, the pinned Codex version and Codex's own hooks/list trust answer, fails closed with code 7, and records diagnostics beside the attempt.

verifier_missed: An attestation failure reserves the next round with no fresh `--main-approve`. When validate_attestation raises (mismatch, downgrade record, or an unattested Claude round), _consume sets retry and calls _reserve with the previous expected revision. The new round record is stamped main_approval {approved: true, at: <retry time>} (subfleet/gate/service.py:244-246, 373-378, 415-416); the round cap stops it (407-409). Test: tests/fake/test_gate_end_to_end.py:134.

A blocked merge permanently holds its operation key, so the same head cannot be merged through the gate again. Merge actions are keyed repository:number:head (subfleet/gate/merge.py:300). An existing key returns its terminal result instead of submitting (313-319), and continue_gate on the same approval only reconciles it (subfleet/gate/service.py:452-458). Merging needs a new head and a fresh peer round (tests/unit/test_gate_service.py:199). Reusing a head with a different base or merge method is refused (merge.py:313-318; tests/unit/test_gate_merge.py:201). Computed: 16 of 25 merge actions were blocked as drafts, so each of those PRs needed a new commit to merge through a gate.

Gate peer jobs never notify a session. The gate submission sets no caller_session (subfleet/gate/round.py:66-72), so the terminal notice is written with session_id NULL (subfleet/daemon.py:2383-2384). Session delivery selects only `WHERE session_id=?` (subfleet/daemon.py:1983; subfleet/hooks.py:383). A gate advances only when a client calls gate.poll or gate.continue (subfleet/gate/cli.py:126-128; subfleet/gate/service.py:319-337). This is why 8 gates sit in reviewing with finished peer jobs.

`subfleet gate` can block with no limit. Its poll loop has no overall deadline (subfleet/gate/cli.py:126-128). max_wall_s counts from started_at (subfleet/daemon.py:3247-3249, 4163), so a peer job queued for capacity never times out. Observed: at 2026-09-28T00:37Z the peer job of gate 20260928-003714-plan-0cae4aae was queued.

Completing a gate, including the merge it authorizes, happens in whichever client first polls. `gate continue <id>` without `--main-approve` on a reviewing gate goes to poll, then _consume, then _complete, then MergeActions.execute. That runs the merge authorized at start (subfleet/gate/service.py:431-440, 319-323, 286-309).

A gate can be left in `agreed` without a certificate. _complete calls capture, which calls verify_pr_workspace. A GateError there (checkout moved off the PR head, or a dirty worktree) is not caught in _complete, so it propagates out of poll as an error, and the gate stays agreed with no certificate (subfleet/gate/service.py:78-84, 286-302, 319-323; subfleet/gate/merge.py:90-95). Only a changed revision is turned into `blocked` (service.py:293-298). Computed: one gate (20260924-181052-pr-d62c432c) is in this state; its specific cause was not established.

The hook misses two more bypasses. A codex global option before the subcommand (`codex -m x exec`, `codex --model gpt exec`) passes, and so does `env` with options other than `--` (subfleet/hooks.py:650-653, 664; computed). `codex --help` documents `codex [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>` (observed).

Overlay drift is locked in by a test. tests/unit/test_guard_overlay.py:149-160 pins private/guard/never-rules-hook.sh and TRUST to their original SHA-256 digests. Porting the Claude hook's newer rules therefore means changing a reviewed pin and the TRUST hook_sha256 that load_guard checks (subfleet/guard/preflight.py:211-212), not just editing the overlay.

The doctor's never-rules check is weak. It passes on any substring 'never-rules', 'never_rules' or 'subfleet-guard' anywhere in ~/.claude/settings.json, and it reads no lane's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (subfleet/doctor.py:348-368). All 17 Claude lanes are keychain-token lanes today (observed).
The family check exists only at gate start, and `--main-model` must be a policy short name (subfleet/gate/service.py:208-216). GateContinueArgs has no main_model field (subfleet/protocol.py:148-160).

The client-side `gate continue --dry-run` reads the gate.json file projection through certificate.load_state (subfleet/gate/service.py:92; subfleet/gate/certificate.py:43-50), not the SQLite journal that the daemon treats as authoritative (service.py:133-143). After a failed projection write it can show stale state.

`gate continue` can raise a gate's round limit up to the policy cap. round_limit uses the new --max-rounds value when one is given and falls back to the stored limit otherwise (subfleet/gate/service.py:59-67, 472).
open_questions: Does a workspace-write run on a keychain-token Claude lane load the hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json, including guard-never-rules.sh and the subfleet PreToolUse guard? The adapter relies on it (subfleet/adapters/claude.py:1297-1300), but that is Claude Code's config resolution, not verified this session. Relatedly, do read-only lanes launched with --setting-sources "" run with no never-rules hook at all?

Can an isolated Astra peer read the PR checkout? The review root is not in the Codex argv (subfleet/adapters/codex.py:433-440); only the prompt names the path, and the Codex read-only sandbox's read scope was not verified.

Why 8 gates stopped in reviewing and 1 in agreed after their peer jobs finished: the gate CLI has no overall deadline (subfleet/gate/cli.py:126-128), but whether callers died on the Bash tool cap, session end or something else is not established.
Whether the one squash merge recorded as merged_revision_mismatch (axiom-rules-engine #184) was a real mismatch or the base advancing between preflight and merge was not determined.

Whether leaving bin/codex out of the wheel (pyproject.toml:28, 32-33) is an intentional retirement of the PATH shim or an installer gap: no installer code covering it was found under tools/ or subfleet/.

Notice states are pending, offered, acknowledged and surfaced; notice.mark sets offered or surfaced (or acknowledged) and never overwrites an acknowledged row; notice.pending returns rows in pending or offered.

The PostToolUse[Bash] hook asks the daemon for the session's still-running jobs (narrowed to the job a `subfleet run` in that Bash call printed), takes a per-job flock lease so only one hook waits on a job, long-polls `wait` in slices of at most 60 s for up to timeout minus 5 s, and on a finish prints the notice text on stderr, marks it `offered` with transport hook:PostToolUse and exits 2; on timeout or any error it exits 0 silently.
claims.checked: subfleet/hooks.py:491-505 (_candidates), 508-541 (post_tool_use), 552-582 (_wait_and_deliver), 585-606 (_deliver), 257-309 (Lease), 119-122; subfleet/contracts.py:242; subfleet/contracts.py:162-165 (Exit.INVALID_INPUT = 2); tests/unit/test_hooks.py:460, 485, 499, 521, 595, 615
claims.correction: PostToolUse[Bash] lists the session's running non-turn jobs, newest first (hooks.py:493). It narrows them to the ids that the tool output names only when the command contains `subfleet run` in command position. When nothing matches it falls back to every running job (hooks.py:496-505; test at tests/unit/test_hooks.py:615). It then waits on the first job whose flock lease it can take, so one hook waits on one job (hooks.py:527-536). It long-polls `wait` in slices of at most 60 s, for at most the hook timeout minus 5 s, which is 595 s by default (hooks.py:525, 552-582). When the job is terminal, it writes to stderr the text of the job's pending/offered notice rows, marks them `offered` with transport hook:PostToolUse, then exits 2. If no such row remains (for example, a prompt hook already surfaced it), it still exits 2 with a summary built from the job row that says 'no notice row for this job', and marks nothing (hooks.py:585-606, 335-348; tests/unit/test_hooks.py:499). On timeout or a daemon/protocol/OS error it exits 0 silently.

additions.name: Notice ledger in the store
additions.description: Completion notices are rows in a `notices` table (states pending, offered, surfaced, acknowledged; acknowledged is terminal), written by the daemon in the transaction that makes a job terminal and read and marked through daemon ops, not per-session JSONL files.

additions.name: Hook-based completion path
additions.description: A PostToolUse[Bash] hook with asyncRewake long-polls one running job per hook under a flock lease and exits 2 with the notice, which Claude Code turns into a task notification that starts a turn; SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit surface whatever is still pending or offered.

additions.name: Single-reader wait hub
additions.description: All `wait` long polls, including hook waits, register with one hub thread that reads job state once per store commit (0.1 s generation poll, 1 s recheck) instead of one read per waiter.

additions.name: Service notices and ping
additions.description: `ping` writes a jobless row to `service_notices` that the session hooks print alongside job notices; the sessions kit's nudges and the daemon's timer alerts use this channel.

additions.name: Launchd-supervised daemon with internal timers
additions.description: One KeepAlive launchd agent runs the daemon, which schedules probe, reset-credit, alert, keepalive, mirror and retention work on its own worker pools.

additions.name: Subfleet-launched process filter
additions.description: Hooks detect processes Subfleet launched (SUBFLEET_ATTEMPT/SUBFLEET_JOB) and there surface only job notices and never spawn a nudge worker, keeping pings and nudges out of lane runs and conversation turns.

additions.name: Retention pins undelivered notices
additions.description: Retention keeps any job whose notice is still pending or offered for a named session and deletes notices only with their job; surfaced or acknowledged service notices are deleted after 14 days.

verifier_cell_problems: Completion signal cell: 'SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit print every `pending` or `offered` row as added context and mark it `surfaced`' is false for service notices (pings, nudges, alerts). They are printed but stay `pending`, so they are re-printed at every later prompt (CS-c22). Say that job notices are marked surfaced and service notices never leave pending. Inside a Subfleet-launched process only job notices are printed (hooks.py:438-439).

Completion signal cell: 'prints the notice on stderr, exits 2 and marks it `offered`' reverses the order. The mark comes before the exit (hooks.py:595-606). The hook also exits 2 with a job-row summary when no notice row remains (hooks.py:590-594).

Completion signal cell: '`subfleet wait` ... exits 124 on `--timeout`' overreaches. The exit is the maximum per-job code, so a cancelled job (130) or a lost one (125) alongside a still-running one wins over 124 (cli.py:1247-1274).

Completion signal cell: 'No socket push remains; nothing imports `notify_push.py`' should read 'no production code imports it'. Its unit test does (tests/unit/test_notify_push.py:20), and its own docstring still calls it layer 4 of delivery (notify_push.py:1-9).
Completion signal cell: 'Of 409 ... 283 had been surfaced or acknowledged on 2026-09-27' should carry the query time, 2026-09-28 00:22 UTC. The table is live: the same query at 00:38 UTC gave 288.

Completion signal cell omits a wake path that callers use: `subfleet wait <id>` under run_in_background, which `run` recommends (cli.py:832, 1081). A reader of 'Claude Code hooks deliver it' would think the hooks are the only path.

Completion signal change_from_v1: the v1 half (inbox push, transcript confirmation, 300 s re-push, lost state, `claude -p --resume` host, Telegram) rests only on the 2026-09-17 doc's v1 column (retired tree) and cannot be re-verified here. The v2 half is supported: there is no lost state in the schema (store_schema.sql:166), grep finds no 'telegram' in subfleet/, and nothing imports notify_push.

Outside a session cell: '`-d`, `--attach` and `SUBFLEET_RUN_DETACH` override' blurs two decisions. -d and SUBFLEET_RUN_DETACH choose the mode, while --attach forces an inline wait in every mode (cli.py:802).

Outside a session cell: 'A job submitted outside a session names no caller session ... 120 of 529 finished-job notices were in that state' misattributes the 120. 112 are gate-review jobs, which never carry caller_session even from inside a session (gate/round.py:66-72); only 8 are sessionless dispatches. The date should also be 2026-09-28 00:22 UTC.

Outside a session cell: '... a keepalive every 18,300 s ... and retention hourly' overreaches for both timers. Keepalive's first due resets to start + 18,300 s on every daemon start (timers.py:102-110) and has not run since 2026-09-27T04:41:47Z (observed). Retention is hourly only after a successful pass. Since 2026-09-27T08:07:21Z it has timed out on every try and been re-offered about every 2 minutes (daemon.py:2415-2421, 2519-2522; computed).

Outside a session cell: 'the reset-credit and alert passes inside it' should note two things. The reset-credit evaluation is skipped when every Codex probe is a network error (timers.py:614-620). Under the live policy (reset_credits.enabled false) it returns 'disabled' (actions.py:256-259).

Addition 'Retention pins undelivered notices': 'surfaced or acknowledged service notices are deleted after 14 days' is true of the SQL (daemon.py:2517-2518). In practice it deletes nothing: no service notice ever leaves `pending`, and every retention pass since 2026-09-27T08:07:21Z has raised before reaching that statement.

Addition 'Service notices and ping' leaves out two users of the channel: `doctor --live` pings, addressed to 'operator' (doctor.py:474), and session-to-session `subfleet ping --session` messages (observed: 32 non-nudge rows addressed to sessions, all pending).
verifier_missed: Gate peer jobs never carry a caller session. gate/round.py:66-72 builds SubmitArgs(kind='gate-review', ...) without caller_session, so every gate-review notice is sessionless: 112 of the 120 sessionless notices (computed). Retention also protects every gate-review job for ever (retention.py:94-95), so those jobs and their notices are never pruned.

The keepalive timer resets at every daemon start. Timers.start sets each interval timer's first due to start + interval (timers.py:102-110), so a daemon restarted more often than every 5 h 5 min never runs keepalive. Observed: `subfleet status --json` shows keepalive last_run 2026-09-27T04:41:47Z and next_due 2026-09-28T02:53:30Z, which is the current daemon's process start (21:48:29Z per `ps -o lstart`) plus 18,300 s.

A failing retention pass retries about every 2 minutes rather than hourly. _control offers retention while _last_maintenance is over an hour old (daemon.py:2491-2492), and only a completed pass updates it (2519-2522). A pass that raises is re-offered on the paced worker retry clock, which also re-arms its next_due (daemon.py:2415-2421). Computed: 228 consecutive TimeoutErrors after 2026-09-27T08:07:21Z, median gap 121 s.

Background `subfleet wait` is a second wake path that callers are told to use. `run` prints 'done → subfleet wait <id> (blocks; ok under run_in_background)' (cli.py:832, 1081), and Claude Code posts a task notification when that background command exits. Observed: 14 such task-notification turns since 2026-09-25, beside the 132 PostToolUse wakes. `wait` acknowledges nothing, so the same job is surfaced again at the next prompt (CS-c16).

PostToolUse can deliver a finished job twice. When a job's notice has already been surfaced, _deliver still writes a summary built from the job row ('no notice row for this job — subfleet runs show <id>') and exits 2 (hooks.py:585-594, 335-348; tests/unit/test_hooks.py:499).
The offline fallback of the session hooks reads only the `notices` table (hooks.py:368-389). While the daemon is down, service notices are not shown at all.

Service pings addressed to a Subfleet-launched session (a lane run or a conversation turn) are never shown, because the hooks there keep only rows that name a job (hooks.py:438-439). tests/e2e/test_conversations.py:234-277 asserts that such a ping stays pending. Pings between interactive sessions share the never-retired defect (observed: 32 non-nudge session rows, all pending).
`doctor --live` writes a service notice with text 'doctor' to 'operator' on every run (doctor.py:471-474). Computed: 5 such rows pending.

Unverified: transcripts since 2026-09-25 hold 360 hook_cancelled attachments for PostToolUse:Bash. The attachment does not name the command, and settings.json has five PostToolUse hooks, three of them matched to Bash. Subfleet's is the only long-running one (timeout 600, asyncRewake), but these cancellations cannot be attributed to it from the record. If they are its own, a cancelled waiter leaves the notice pending for layer 3, which is safe.
open_questions: Does SessionStart additionalContext start a model turn on its own? It appears not: in session 7638e341 the turn after the SessionStart nudge began from a cross-session message, not from the hook. The harness code was not read to confirm this.
The v2 docs (C-15.2) describe a layer-4 socket push that the code never wires in. Should notify_push.py be wired into the daemon or deleted, and its docstrings corrected either way?
Where should timer alerts go? Options are a real alerts.operator_session, or a Telegram or chief-of-staff path; nothing is configured today.

Why has the retention pass timed out since 2026-09-27T08:07Z? This belongs to the durability row and was not investigated here. Separately, 110 pending notices addressed to sessions (24 older than 3 days) pin their jobs against retention indefinitely.
The `subfleet wait` under run_in_background path relies on Claude Code's own background-task notification (hinted at subfleet/cli.py:832). That is harness behaviour and was not verified in code here.

claims.claim: Inside the reserving transaction, the fleet count covers attempts of the job's pool (turn or detached) in state reserved, starting, running or finalizing. `saturated[pool]` is set when that count reaches the pool cap.

During route evaluation, detached attempts in flight plus probe leases at or above max_active_attempts add the capacity block 'fleet', which refuses every lane. Probe leases are all leases whose holder starts with 'probe:'.

The per-lane detached cap is max_in_flight_per_lane (2) when the lane has a fresh provider reading. Without one it is min(max_in_flight_per_lane, max_in_flight_unmeasured, 1), so the unmeasured cap can never exceed 1.

claims.claim: max_child_jobs (8) is checked at submit against every job ever created with that parent, whatever its state. It is a lifetime child budget, not a concurrency cap.
claims.checked: subfleet/daemon.py:1752-1758 (count(*) FROM jobs WHERE parent_job_id=?); read-only SQL: 1,375 job ids carry a retention.pruned event
claims.correction: max_child_jobs (8) is checked at submit against every job row still in the store with that parent, whatever its state (daemon.py:1756-1758). Retention deletes job rows (1,375 pruned so far), so it is a budget over retained children, not strictly over every child ever created. It is not a concurrency cap.

claims.claim: max_writable_per_session (default 8) limits the live writable jobs one session may hold. It is checked at submit.

No lease enforces a cap. An attempt takes the lowest free `lane:<id>:slot:<n>` lease (a turn takes `slot:turn-<n>`) inside the reserving transaction. The caps are counts of attempt rows, and a lease cannot occupy a slot.
claims.checked: subfleet/daemon.py:3536, 3678-3696; subfleet/capacity.py:374-375, 390-393; contradicted by daemon.py:879-893 and scheduler.py:386, 456-459
claims.correction: Per-lane in_flight counts come only from attempt rows. The slot lease an attempt takes (the lowest free lane:<id>:slot:<n>, or slot:turn-<n> for a turn, daemon.py:3536, 3692-3696) is numbering, not a cap. Probe leases are the exception: they are counted in reserved_probes toward the fleet cap (daemon.py:893, scheduler.py:386), and they make their lane unavailable, so it is rejected no-slot (daemon.py:892, scheduler.py:456-459). 'A lease cannot occupy a slot' is false for probe leases.

claims.claim: Timer probes and admission probes hold `lane:<id>:slot:0`. A lane with any probe lease is marked unavailable and rejected 'no-slot' for that probe's duration.

The reserving transaction re-judges any lane whose rows changed, and every lane of the walk when a fleet or parent cap began or ended. A property test asserts that no reservation exceeds the lane cap, or the pool-plus-probes fleet cap, across interleaved commits.
claims.checked: subfleet/route_check.py:80-226 (still_stands; the every-lane rule on a cap flip is at 201-207, outside the cited 83-167); daemon.py:3466-3479; tests/fake/test_admission_latency.py:180-202 check_reservation (asserts at 199-202); :352 test_c6_3_admission_never_exceeds_a_cap_or_double_books_across_commits
claims.correction: The reserving transaction re-judges the lanes whose rows or clocks changed (route_check.py:148-158, 184-199). When a fleet or parent cap began or ended, it re-judges every lane of the walk (route_check.py:201-207). A Hypothesis property test with 80 derandomized examples asserts, at every reservation, that the lane had room and that pool attempts plus probe leases stayed below max_active_attempts (tests/fake/test_admission_latency.py:199-202, 346-359).

claims.claim: Once recovery completes, the control loop offers the 'admission' and 'admission:turns' passes every tick_s, which is 0.05 s by default and is not overridden by main. A key whose worker is still running is not offered again.

A pass reads queued and waiting jobs ORDER BY created_at,rowid and walks them by tier rank in the policy's declared order (trivial, easy, standard, hard), turns first within a tier, then by created_at. An older hard job is therefore evaluated after newer standard jobs.

'behind-older-job' means the pass held the job without evaluating it, because an older waiter of the same waiter class (the tier, or tier#turn) competes with it. Two jobs compete when their model sets overlap (a pin, or the chain from the job's tier upward) and their lane sets overlap (a lane pin). Unknown on either side counts as overlap.
claims.checked: subfleet/scheduler.py:170-223; daemon.py:3246, 3288-3302, 3375-3389; tests/fake/test_tier_hold_by_demand.py:39, 52, 73
claims.correction: Usually 'behind-older-job' means the job was held at the top of the pass without evaluation, because a competing older waiter of the same class (the tier, or tier#turn) exists (daemon.py:3294-3302). One exception: a transient-retry job whose pinned pair was let go is held 'behind-older-job' after a look and put on a backoff clock (daemon.py:3375-3389). Competition is overlapping model sets and overlapping lane pins, and unknown counts as overlap (scheduler.py:176-223).

claims.claim: A job becomes a waiter in these cases: it has a future capacity clock; its admission probe is pending; its evaluation chose no lane; live attempts reached its limit; a lease it needs is held; or it was left for the next pass after ROUTE_TRIES.

The competition test ignores job exclusions, so head-of-line blocking occurs. An older job whose own `-x` excludes the only lane waits with hold 'excluded', and a newer job for the same model is held 'behind-older-job' while that lane is open with two free slots. The newer job is placed as soon as the older one is cancelled.

claims.claim: 'fleet-full' has two sources. (1) The reserving transaction finds live attempts at or above the pool cap. That also sets saturated[pool], and every later job of that pool in the same pass is then held 'fleet-full' without evaluation. (2) An evaluation rejects every lane only for 'no-slot' while the fleet capacity block is present.
claims.checked: subfleet/daemon.py:3298-3301, 3484-3487, 3499-3504; scheduler.py:757-787; tests/fake/test_tier_hold_by_demand.py:103
claims.correction: 'fleet-full' arises three ways. (1) In the reserving transaction a lane was chosen but live pool attempts are at or above the pool cap (daemon.py:3504). (2) No lane was chosen, and dominant_rejection finds at least one lane (not every lane) rejected only for no-slot while a 'fleet' capacity block is present (scheduler.py:770-786). (3) Any reservation that saw live >= cap sets saturated[pool] (3487). Every later job of that pool in the pass is then held 'fleet-full' without evaluation, unless its wait_reason is in NOT_ADMISSIONS_TO_PLACE (daemon.py:107-108, 3298-3301).

claims.claim: 'slot-kept': while an older waiter of the same tier exists, a job that passes it may reserve only up to pool cap minus 1, which leaves the last slot to the waiter.
A capacity wait's next check comes 1 s after the look, doubling with each consecutive identical verdict up to 30 s. A known reset that comes sooner moves the check earlier.
A lease that was held at the previous pass and is gone now brings capacity waits forward to this pass. A probe wait keeps its own 60 s clock and is never brought forward.

A lane is 'open' in status when it is owned by v2, enabled, not the desktop login, not identity-mismatched, under no account-scoped closure, below its slot cap, and not in unavailable_lanes (a probe lease or a latched credential). Admission can still refuse an open lane, for a model-scoped closure, the headroom floor, the reserve or the job's exclusions.
claims.checked: subfleet/capacity.py:429-448; timers.py:563-564 (credential-latched); scheduler.py:382-387, 433-459
claims.correction: open_lanes lists v2-owned, enabled, non-desktop, non-identity-mismatched lanes with no account-scoped closure, detached in_flight below the lane's slot cap, and no entry in unavailable_lanes (a probe lease, or a latched credential from timers.py:563-564). It does not check the fleet cap or the parent cap. So a lane can be 'open' while every job is refused 'fleet-full' or 'parent-cap'. Admission can also refuse an open lane for a model-scoped closure, the headroom floor, the reserve, the job's exclusions, allow_desktop, or (for turns) config-dir and the turn slot pool (scheduler.py:433-482).

claims.claim: route_evaluations counts reservation checks, held in memory since daemon start. 'reused': the check kept the early decision's lane and model. 'rechosen': it chose again from the lanes that changed. 'rejudged': lanes judged again. 'moved': the pin names another lane, an evaluation would raise, or the rows or policy are gone. 'old': the clock stepped back. 'error': the check raised. 'again': re-evaluations off the lock after a refusal. 'deferred': jobs left for the next pass after 3 tries.

additions.name: Admission queue with tier-FIFO and competition-scoped holds
additions.description: Pending jobs sit in SQLite and are placed by passes that walk tiers in policy order, FIFO within each. A job is held only behind an older waiter it competes with: an overlapping model and an overlapping pinned lane, where unknown counts as overlap. Jobs in different tiers never wait on each other.

additions.name: Fleet, lane, turn and parent caps
additions.description: Detached attempts: max_active_attempts (4 shipped, 16 live), with probe leases counted during evaluation. Per lane: 2 with a fresh reading, 1 without. Turns: 3 fleet-wide and 1 per lane, in a separate pool with slot leases `slot:turn-<n>`. Parents: all descendants share max_active_attempts_per_parent, default 1. At submit: max_child_jobs 8 (lifetime) and max_writable_per_session 8.

additions.name: slot-kept
additions.description: A job that passes an older waiting job of its tier may use at most cap minus 1 slots, so the waiter can start as soon as its capacity appears.

additions.name: Capacity-wait backoff with lease-freed expedite
additions.description: A repeated verdict is rechecked after 1 s, doubling to a 30 s ceiling, and adds no new decision row. A lease released since the last pass brings the next look forward. Probe waits keep a fixed 60 s clock.

additions.name: Reservation-time route check and route_evaluations counters
additions.description: The route is evaluated off the store lock. The reserving transaction re-judges only the lanes whose rows or clocks changed, or every lane when a cap flips. It retries up to 3 times and otherwise leaves the job 'route-moved'. The outcomes are counted in status.admission.route_evaluations.

additions.name: Admission visibility: status.admission, open_lanes and why
additions.description: status reports pending count, hold reasons, open lanes and idle time. `why <job>` prints the hold, the recheck history and the recorded decision, or evaluates the job on demand if admission never did. daemon.log warns when lanes are open and nothing is placed for a reason outside the expected holds.

verifier_cell_problems: Concurrency v2_cell: 'The live ~/.subfleet/policy.json sets 16 and replaces the default file whole (daemon.py:480-484)'. It replaces default_policy.json, but load_policy merges DEFAULT_CAPS under the file's caps (policy.py:218-219), and CONVERSATION_DEFAULTS and RETENTION_DEFAULTS too (policy.py:311-327). max_writable_per_session 8 and the workspace timeouts therefore apply under the live file, which does not set them.

Concurrency v2_cell: 'A lane takes 2 detached attempts while it has a provider reading under 120 s old'. The reading must be provider-labelled, numeric, not future-dated and not past its resets_at (capacity.py:236-248). It may be of any scope on the lane (scheduler.py:452). The cell also leaves out what made the per-lane cap the binding limit at the snapshot: detached attempts were 14 against a cap of 16, yet every lane was no-slot because none was measured.

Concurrency v2_cell: 'Detached attempts ... peaked at 16 on 2026-09-27'. The events-based peak was at 2026-09-27T02:59:44Z. That is before the current live policy (f717de82) was first used at 21:48:31Z, so a cap of at least 16 was already set under the previous policy (78e3b076, from 09-26T13:26:50Z). Do not imply the current live file introduced 16. The interval also runs from attempt.starting to the first attempt.finalizing, while the cap counts reserved through finalizing (daemon.py:3484-3486).

Admission v2_cell: 'time to first placement has had a p50 of 2.2 min and a p90 of 1.9 h'. This is submit to first attempt.starting, over the 1,153 jobs that started. It leaves out the 233 jobs cancelled before any attempt started, which had waited p50 557 s and p90 6,934 s by cancellation (computed from job.submitted and job.cancel_requested events), and the jobs still pending. Say so, or the distribution reads shorter than the queue was.

Admission v2_cell: 'Once one reservation finds the pool full, every later job in that pass is held fleet-full'. It applies only to later jobs of the same pool (turn or detached), and a job whose wait_reason is in NOT_ADMISSIONS_TO_PLACE keeps that reason (daemon.py:107-108, 3298-3301).

Additions, 'Admission queue with tier-FIFO...': 'Jobs in different tiers never wait on each other' overreaches. They never hold each other 'behind-older-job', but they share the fleet and lane caps. Lower tiers are evaluated first in every pass (scheduler.py:155-167). saturated[pool] holds later jobs of every tier (daemon.py:3298-3301). slot-kept keeps a slot only for waiters of the same class (daemon.py:3491).
Additions, 'Admission visibility': cites render.py:175-240, but why_queue is render.py:206-249 (with _blocked at 198-204).

defect-0-2 is presented as a defect, but the code documents it as intended: daemon.py:2012-2016 says a job held behind an older one has no decision row and `why` evaluates it on demand. It is a visibility limitation of status.admission.reasons, not a bug.

defect-0-3: the counts are mostly historical (98,059 of 110,762 from 09-20 and 09-21). As written, the entry implies an ongoing rate, which is about 600 to 3,100 a day since 09-22. The stronger present-day point it misses is that no attempt.reserved event ever carries an attempt_id.

defect-0-4: the 'clamp to 1' difference has no effect at current values (max_in_flight_unmeasured is 1 both shipped and live). The material differences are that dispatchable also requires the fleet cap to be unmet and the account headroom floor (timers.py:583, 590), and that it excludes a lane with any closure (586-587). open_lanes checks neither the fleet cap nor headroom.
defect-1-5: 'No lease or process-list estimate occupies a slot' conflicts with C-c16. Probe leases block the lane and count toward the fleet cap.

Concurrency change_from_v1: '35 runs overlapped' and 'in_flight was only a sort tiebreak' come from the 2026-09-17 v1 doc (docs/native-workflows-vs-subfleet.md:113). Label them as v1 measurements from that doc; they cannot be re-verified against the v2 tree.
verifier_missed: Busy lanes are never probed, so their second slot depends on readings from their own attempts. The periodic probe reserves through timers._reserve, which skips any lane with an attempt in reserved, starting, running or finalizing (timers.py:332-333, 401-403, 593-600). Since cutover, Claude lanes' only provider-labelled readings came from attempts' rate_limit_event (979). The periodic Claude probe wrote 3,390 'unknown' and 282 'admission-observed' readings and no 'provider' reading. Codex 'wham' probe readings (39,504, all with attempt_id NULL) come only from idle lanes. (Computed: read-only `SELECT substr(lane_id,1,5),source,label,count(*) FROM readings GROUP BY 1,2,3`.) A busy lane is therefore unmeasured within 120 s of its last attempt reading and takes at most 1 more attempt (scheduler.py:452-455). At 00:20Z this, not the fleet cap, held all 35 jobs: 14 detached attempts against a cap of 16, and every lane no-slot.

The detached admission pass is serial, and each job's slow steps block every later job in the pass. Workspace preparation runs inline (daemon.py:3325), with git calls capped at 60 s and `git worktree add` at 180 s (contracts.py:191-192). The admission probe also runs synchronously inside the pass: the comment says 'The admission worker serializes probes' (daemon.py:2981-2983, 3031), and the probe record's deadline is 60 s (3005). One pass per kind runs at a time (daemon.py:556, 3077-3079). The store holds 638 probe.reserved events.

Cross-tier ordering is strict with no aging. Each pass evaluates trivial, easy, standard, then hard (scheduler.py:155-167), so lower tiers take free slots first on every pass. slot-kept reserves a slot only for a waiter of the same class (daemon.py:3491), so an older hard job gets no reserved slot against newer standard jobs.

There is a 'parent-cap' hold label. dominant_rejection returns it when the rejections are room-only and a parent: capacity block is present (scheduler.py:784-787). It is in EXPECTED_HOLDS (daemon.py:110). The parent cap counts only descendants, never the parent's own attempt, because ancestors() starts from parent_job_id (scheduler.py:233-239).

The exclusion head-of-line blocking generalizes, by deduction from code (not executed). competes() compares only model sets and lane pins (scheduler.py:216-223). Any refusal specific to the older job can therefore hold back a newer job an open lane would take. Examples are allow_desktop (scheduler.py:435-436) and, for turns, config-dir (437-440). Such a stall is logged as a WARNING after 60 s when the older job's hold is outside EXPECTED_HOLDS (daemon.py:102, 110-111, 3180-3187).

One job holds at most one live attempt. This is checked before workspace preparation (daemon.py:3321-3323) and again inside the reserving transaction, including quarantined attempts (3462-3467), and gives the hold 'attempt-live'.

The wall clock counts from first placement. The pass kills a queued job, such as a transient retry, whose started_at is more than max_wall_s old (daemon.py:3247-3249), because started_at is set once at the first reservation (3597).

claims.claim: Attempts are created at admission, not at submit. Admission inserts an attempts row in state 'reserved' and a decisions row, and moves the job to 'running'.

Further attempts of the same job are made only while seq < max_attempts, and only when the attempt was lost on a read-only job, limited on an unpinned job, or transient. max_attempts defaults to caps.max_attempts = 3 in both the shipped and the live policy.

claims.correction: Two code paths make further attempts, and both require seq < max_attempts. (1) When an attempt ends, the job is retried only if it was not cancelled and the attempt was lost on a read-only job, LIMITED on an unpinned job, or TRANSIENT. A pinned job retries a transient failure only if no earlier attempt was transient (`subfleet/daemon.py:4750-4754`). (2) An attempt that never launched puts the job back to 'queued' whenever it was not cancelled and seq < max_attempts, pinned or not (`daemon.py:4393-4403`). max_attempts defaults to caps.max_attempts = 3 in both the shipped and the live policy (`daemon.py:1292-1295`; `subfleet/default_policy.json:109`; observed). claims.claim: A manifest holds at most 256 entries, and the daemon independently rejects a batch label whose index or size falls outside 1 <= index <= size <= 256.
Each manifest key maps to one `run` option. Relative paths resolve against the manifest's directory. Precedence is entry, then manifest defaults, then the command line's own flags.
Every entry is validated before anything is sent. An invalid entry, or one without exactly one of prompt or prompt_text, ends the command with nothing submitted.
A batch is not one daemon request. The CLI sends one `submit` per entry, sequentially, each through call_settled.
When the daemon refuses an entry, the rest still run. The refused row records outcome 'refused' with rc, error and fix, and the exit code is the first failure's.

An entry whose answer is lost twice, unreadable or missing a job id stops the batch. Later entries are reported 'not-sent', and the command prints the `run --batch FILE --request-id <batch id>` re-run that settles them. A daemon gone at connect also stops it, with exit 69.
claims.checked: subfleet/cli.py:1002-1004, 1010-1055, 1083-1091; subfleet/client.py:462-509 (sources of OutcomeUnknown); subfleet/contracts.py:171 (DAEMON_UNAVAILABLE = 69); cli.py:406-407
claims.correction: The batch stops on an entry whose outcome is unknown (`subfleet/cli.py:1010-1020`). additions.name: run --batch FILE
additions.description: Sends up to 256 `run` invocations from one TOML or JSON manifest (label, defaults, jobs). Every entry is validated first. After that each entry gets its own `submit`, and a refused entry does not stop the others. Entry request ids are <batch id>-<n>, so re-running the same manifest with --request-id <batch id> creates no job twice. Entries are independent, and no entry can depend on another.

additions.name: --request-id idempotence
additions.description: Each job row carries a unique request id and a SHA-256 payload digest. A repeat with the same digest returns the existing job (created=false). A repeat with a different digest is refused with exit 2 and names the job. The client re-sends a lost submit once under the same id and settles a refused re-send by looking the id up. Deduplication lasts only as long as the job row is retained.

additions.name: Parent/child job relation
additions.description: --parent links a job to a parent. Cancelling the parent cancels every dependent descendant, and --independent children are spared along with their subtrees. A child cannot be added under a cancelled parent unless it is independent. A parent takes at most 8 children, and all descendants share one active-attempt slot by default. This is the only job-to-job relation in the store.

additions.name: Conversation turns as jobs
additions.description: The daemon turns each conversation message into a 'turn' job, one attempt each, with its own admission pool. Callers cannot submit turn jobs directly. This is v2's only multi-turn construct besides gate rounds.

additions.name: Gate rounds as daemon jobs
additions.description: `gate` runs inside the daemon (gate.start, gate.poll and gate.continue ops). Each round is a pinned, isolated, read-only gate-review job with max_attempts=1. Rounds are capped by caps.gate_max_rounds (4) instead of being unlimited.

It marks the attempt failed with outcome_class 'unknown' and requeues the job (state 'queued') whenever it was not cancelled and seq < max_attempts, whatever its pin or sandbox. Submit does not check `kind` against contracts.JOB_KINDS (`subfleet/contracts.py:312`). jobs.kind is TEXT NOT NULL with no CHECK (`subfleet/store_schema.sql:70`). daemon.submit special-cases only turn, resume, revive and gate-review (`subfleet/daemon.py:1163`, `1181-1189`, `1221-1232`), so a socket caller can store any other kind string. `grep -rn JOB_KINDS subfleet` finds only contracts.py:312 and cli.py:55 and 2759.

`kill` on a parent that has already ended returns 'already finished' before the recursive walk (`subfleet/daemon.py:2344-2345`). A finished parent therefore cannot be used to cancel children that are still running.

Retention never deletes the state store's events. retention.py deletes artifacts, readings, notices, decisions, attempts and jobs (`subfleet/retention.py:384-387`); `grep -rn 'DELETE FROM events' subfleet` finds only `conversations/store.py:1197`, which is a different database. job.submitted events and batch labels therefore outlive their job rows: computed, 1,476 job.submitted events against 602 job rows.

The daemon validates batch labels one entry at a time (`subfleet/daemon.py:1582-1597`) and never checks that a batch's entries all arrive. Computed over job.submitted events with a batch label: 6 of 44 batch ids have fewer submitted jobs than their declared size, so 13 of 198 declared entries never created a job. One 17-entry batch has 9. Query: python3 over sqlite3 ro, SELECT job_id,data_json FROM events WHERE kind='job.submitted' AND data_json LIKE '%"batch"%', grouped by batch.id and compared with max(batch.size).

Gate rounds are chained outside the jobs table. Gate state lives in gates/<id>/gate.json and in 'gate.state' events (`subfleet/gate/service.py:92`, `131-158`). A new round cannot be submitted while another round of the same gate is queued, waiting or running, or holds its lease (`subfleet/daemon.py:1741-1751`). Retention never prunes gate-review jobs (`subfleet/retention.py:94`), so their request ids stay deduplicated.

`run --batch` refuses -p or a positional prompt, and refuses --dry-run/--why (`subfleet/cli.py:942-945`; `tests/unit/test_cli_batch.py:154` test_c17_7_flags_that_mean_one_job_are_refused). A batch cannot be previewed as a whole.

The two admission pools also shape control flow: turn jobs are admitted against conversations.max_active_turns (default 3 in code, set in neither policy file) instead of caps.max_active_attempts (`subfleet/scheduler.py:383-387`; `subfleet/daemon.py:3243`, `3296-3297`; `subfleet/policy.py:77`).
open_questions: Whether any dispatch job ever used --parent cannot be settled from the store. The 602 retained rows show parents only on 3 resume jobs, and job.submitted events do not record parent_job_id for the 874 pruned jobs.

The declared batch sizes sum to 198, but only 185 entries have a job.submitted event. The missing 13 were refused, not sent, or re-sent under existing ids, and the store records no event for any of these, so the split is unknown.

The run --batch CLI tests (tests/unit/test_cli_batch.py, tests/unit/test_outcome_unknown.py c17_7 cases) could not be executed here. The extract lives under /private/tmp, and the CLI's C-2.4 check refuses workdirs there, so 7 test_cli_batch and 24 test_outcome_unknown cases failed with 'a workdir under /tmp is refused'. The batch claims rest on code reading. The daemon-level tests for C-6.2 and C-7.3 and the scheduler parent-cap test passed.
Is a lifetime (not live) max_child_jobs count intended? The plan docs were not consulted as evidence.

additions.name: Guardian launch gate
additions.description: The guardian spawns the provider only after the daemon has committed its pid, pgid, boot id and process start, so a daemon crash between spawn and commit can never leave an unrecorded provider running.

additions.name: Boot-aware process identity
additions.description: Liveness compares pid, process start and the kernel boot-session UUID, returns 'unknown' instead of 'dead' when inspection fails, and gates every signal, so pid reuse or a reboot is never read as the recorded guardian.

additions.name: Quarantine
additions.description: An attempt whose process census cannot be verified empty is quarantined. Its job ends lost (rc 125), its output and worktree leases are kept, and it stays pinned against retention until an operator runs kill --confirm-dead or --force-release.

additions.name: Replayable finalization
additions.description: The outcome and attestation are frozen in finalization.json and replayed on re-finalization, and pending exports are re-run every tick, so a crash during or after finalization reaches the same result.

additions.name: Idempotent request ids
additions.description: A request id is bound to a payload digest, so a retried submit returns the same job and a changed payload is refused. The CLI mints a fresh id unless --request-id is given.

additions.name: Native resume as a daemon job
additions.description: `subfleet resume` submits a supervised job pinned to the source attempt's lane and model that continues the recorded native session with `--resume` for Claude or the thread id for Codex.

additions.name: Transactional event log and hashed artifacts
additions.description: Each committed state change appends an events row, and each finalized attempt records its deliverable, streams, launch record, prompt and manifest with sha256 and size.

additions.name: Two-pool retention with worktree removal
additions.description: Detached jobs and conversation turns are pruned against separate count and byte budgets. Allocated worktrees are removed with git only when clean or preserved by a matching salvage ref, under a worktree lease that survives a crash.

verifier_cell_problems: Durability cell: 'so a job outlives its caller and a daemon crash (tests/fake/test_daemon_contract.py:79)' cites only the daemon-SIGKILL test; caller-exit survival is test_c5_2_job_survives_submitting_client_exit at tests/fake/test_daemon_contract.py:56.

Durability cell: 'Every tick the daemon re-checks each live attempt by pid, boot id and process start' overreaches. Receipts, cancel and wall clock are read every tick (0.05 s), but process inspection is paced to once per INSPECT_INTERVAL_S = 1 s from a shared table (daemon.py:4194-4235; contracts.py:220), and an 'unknown' liveness decides nothing (4267-4272).

Durability cell: 'a dead guardian without one becomes lost' holds only on a verified-empty census. Otherwise the group is killed with killed_by='recovery' and can end quarantined (daemon.py:4280-4284, 4415-4461).

Durability cell: 'Nothing needs a manual reap' overreaches. A quarantined attempt keeps its out: and worktree leases, and stays pinned against retention, until an operator runs kill --confirm-dead or --force-release (daemon.py:4474, 4480-4501; retention.py:99). A finalization that raises is retried without limit (daemon.py:2408-2425).
Durability cell: 'quarantines the attempt and ends the job lost' should add: or cancelled, rc 130, when a cancel was requested (daemon.py:4475).

Durability change_from_v1: 'v1 finalized a run only from the runner's EXIT trap and left the rest to a manual runs reap' and 'adds lost and quarantined outcomes' cite nothing. The v1 tree is not the v2 extract and cannot be checked from these citations.

Audit cell: 'Every store transaction that changes a row appends an events row' is true per transaction or savepoint, but nested transactions each append one. One helper write usually leaves two rows, and add_event leaves a payload row plus '{}' (store.py:231-237, 501-508, 746-749); 534,038 of 782,484 events have empty payloads.

Audit cell: 'Each placement stores the full routing decision beside its attempt' is true but not representative: 33,088 of 33,638 decision rows are attempt-less hold and probe rows (daemon.py:3042, 3513).

Audit cell: 'against 500 detached jobs or 2 GiB' should say 'and': each pool must meet both its count and byte budgets (retention.py:311-314). Turn jobs have their own budgets of 2,000 jobs, 4 GiB and 14 days.

Audit cell: 'It deletes job, attempt, decision, notice and artifact rows and allocated worktrees' omits readings and the jobs/<id> directory. It also overstates the worktree part: only a worktree named by jobs.worktree for a workspace-write, not-in-place job is removed (retention.py:145-157), so a worktree allocated before placement is never collected (daemon.py:3831-3833).

Audit cell: '1,531 of 1,642 recorded passes had hit that deadline' is correct, but timed-out passes still prune jobs they reach before the deadline (47 pruned 2026-09-27T23:30:56Z-23:38:56Z during TimeoutError passes).

Audit change_from_v1: 'v1 wrote a per-run meta.json and an unpruned decisions.jsonl' cites nothing. 'neither the count cap nor the byte cap holds' has no byte computation behind it among the reader's claims. A read-only one gives pinned owned worktrees about 81.8 GiB against the 2 GiB cap, with unpinned ones about 1.7 GiB (du -sk joined to the pin replica).
Defect (v1_item 0, retention caps): 'which is most writable jobs that changed files' is an uncomputed characterization.
Defect (v1_item 0, finished recorded lost): 'more than 3 s after the exit receipt' is wrong about the clock. The settle window starts at the first non-empty census in _finalize (daemon.py:4640).

Defect (v1_item 0, finalization retries): the two attempts cited as stuck succeeded and exported at 00:38:04Z and 00:38:26Z on 2026-09-28. 'Up to 128 times' should read 'at least 128', because the log prints only at powers of two.

Defect (v1_item 3): 'An attempt with no recorded guardian is failed at start grace' misstates the rule. At start grace an attempt with no start or exit receipt is failed on a verified-empty census and quarantined otherwise; a reserved attempt this daemon did not launch is failed at once.
verifier_missed: Worktree leak before placement: _workspace creates worktrees/<job id> before the route is evaluated (subfleet/daemon.py:2651-2670), and jobs.worktree is set only when an attempt is reserved (daemon.py:3597; the code's own comment at 3831-3833). _discard_fresh_worktree runs only on a route refusal (3871). kill of a waiting job with no active attempt makes it cancelled without discarding the tree (2346-2356). Retention removes only worktrees named by jobs.worktree (retention.py:145-157). Observed: live waiting job 20260927-154957-cs-verify-g05 has a directory with jobs.worktree NULL, and orphans ccr3-review-opus and pepy-microdf-estimators were cancelled before any attempt.

Retention deletes files before its final pin re-check: the worktree removal and rmtree of jobs/<id> (subfleet/retention.py:338-355) come before the in-transaction pinned() recheck (381-383). A job that becomes pinned in that window keeps its rows but loses its files.

Events are live runtime state as well as audit. Timers replays every timer.run event at each daemon start (subfleet/timers.py:89-92; 93,514 rows now, about 720 more a day from retention's 2-minute failure cycle with doubled rows), and probe records are read from probe.state events (daemon.py:75-80). So unpruned events also grow startup and lookup work.

Conversation turns attest through a different path, subfleet/conversations/classify.py:112 (TurnAdapter via conversations/service.py:2092-2093), not adapters/claude.py:1791-1863. Five of the 8 '<synthetic>' mismatches are turn attempts, four finalized 2026-09-27T23:27-23:43Z under the current release (sqlite ro).

Decision-row growth is throttled by verdict signature: a hold or probe wait that repeats its verdict adds no decisions row (subfleet/daemon.py:3494-3513, 3035-3042). Rows per day fell from 25,917 on 2026-09-21 to 81-297 since 2026-09-22 (sqlite ro GROUP BY substr(evaluated_at,1,10)).

Every lost job in the store began as a quarantine. The 3 'lost' attempts are the surviving confirm-dead resolutions (daemon.py:4500), so the guardian-loss path (_lost, daemon.py:4503-4504, 4666-4673) has no surviving instance (sqlite ro).

A quarantine keeps every lease except the lane slot (only 'lane:%' is deleted, daemon.py:4474), so the out: path and worktree stay fenced. tests/fake/test_state_contract.py:290 asserts that the out: lease survives. Those leases also pin the job in retention (retention.py:106-109).

Cancelling a job that has no active attempt ends it at once as cancelled (rc 130) with the notice 'cancelled before launch' (subfleet/daemon.py:2346-2356). Cancel recurses to non-independent children (2346).
open_questions: Why does the census's marker read (`ps -axEww -o pid=,command=`) fail? It could be the 10 s subprocess cap under load or a decode error in environment text. procs.containment catches both as 'marker enumeration unavailable', and daemon.log records error types only.
Which SalvageError keeps the two 'finalizing' attempts (20260927-151333-r218-daemon-astra/a1 and 20260927-151314-r218-daemon-opus/a2) from finishing? The log names only the exception type.
How did six allocated worktree directories outlive their pruned job rows? _remove_worktree returns early when the job row has no owned worktree, which is one possible path, but this is not verified.

Do the sessions named by the 230 pending and 16 offered notices still exist? Retention treats any non-empty session id as able to read its notice, so notices for ended sessions pin their jobs indefinitely.
No end-to-end test covers a machine reboot. That a reboot loses running attempts, retries read-only jobs and preserves queued jobs is read from code (procs.liveness, daemon._finalize), not observed.
The pin breakdown in AUD-c21 replicates retention._pins in read-only SQL without the conversation service's pins or the sizing-error pins, so the true pinned count can only be higher.

additions.name: Desktop-lane exclusion (C-10.3)
additions.description: Each capacity view recomputes which Claude lane is the desktop app's account, from the profile endpoint asked with the app's own credential, falling back to the ~/.claude.json email and the last verified label. Admission rejects that lane with reason `desktop` unless the job passed `--allow-desktop`, and re-checks the flag inside the probe reservation. It replaced v1's 10-point handicap. Codex lanes are never marked desktop.

additions.name: Identity binding (C-10.6)
additions.description: The adapter compares the account a lane's credential reports with the lane's recorded identity. A mismatched lane gets no capacity from its readings, is rejected, is disabled, and is released only by re-enrolment under a new lane id.

additions.name: Scoped closures with clock provenance
additions.description: A limit becomes a closure with a reason, an account or model scope taken from the provider's own rate-limit event, and a reported or guessed (now + 3600 s) clock. Operators can add account-scope holds with `lanes hold`, and a held lane is still probed.

additions.name: Measured versus unmeasured lanes
additions.description: Only a fresh provider reading, at most 120 s old, gives a lane its second slot and a headroom rank. An unmeasured lane takes one attempt and ranks last. Expensive unmeasured work first runs a same-model admission probe on the lane.

additions.name: Provider-specific lane ranking
additions.description: Codex lanes are spent in order of earliest weekly reset. Claude lanes rank stranded capacity first (a lane whose higher-priority model is closed), then worst-window headroom or reserve slack, then fewer attempts in flight.

additions.name: One evaluator for every routing path
additions.description: Submission, `why`, the advisory `pick` and the `codex` PATH shim's automatic home choice all call scheduler.evaluate, so the reserve and the desktop exclusion have no side door. The shim also runs `_api-lane-check` on every noninteractive launch.

additions.name: Per-job policy hash
additions.description: Every job records the sha256 of the policy bytes it was evaluated under. Eight distinct policies appear on jobs between the cutover and 2026-09-28.
additions.evidence: subfleet/policy.py:99-101, 337-339; SQL SELECT substr(policy_hash,1,12),count(*) FROM jobs GROUP BY 1

additions.name: Re-enrolment instead of re-enable
additions.description: A disabled lane is never re-enabled. `lanes enroll` on the same credential creates a new lane id, carries over its non-auth closures, and pins on the old id follow to the new one.

additions.name: Timer spend on lanes
additions.description: Besides jobs, lanes pay for keepalive turns (Haiku) and heal turns under expired homes. The periodic Claude probe is an HTTP usage read, not a model turn.

It targets enabled v2 Claude lanes whose stored desktop column is 0, and skips a lane with a request in the last 18,000 s or with a live attempt or lease (timers.py:326-335, 655-661, 688-691). The actual desktop account (claude-4) is therefore eligible, and claude-1 is not.

Whose quota cell: 'The daemon starts without API keys or the caller's OAuth token' is true for `subfleet daemon start` and the launchd plist (cli.py:2075-2083, 2128, 2369-2375). Each launch then re-strips only the API-key variables (daemon.py:2853-2855, 4046-4049), not CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.

Whose quota cell and additions: 'API-key Codex homes are refused at enrolment, at launch and by the codex PATH shim' implies one test, but there are three detectors that disagree (codex.py:115-117; daemon.py:1789-1799; importer.py:666). A home whose auth.json holds only CODEX_API_KEY is refused at enrolment and by the shim but passes the daemon's launch check.

Addition 'One evaluator for every routing path': 'so the reserve and the desktop exclusion have no side door' overreaches. The timers choose lanes for probes, heal turns and Haiku keepalives without scheduler.evaluate, using the stored desktop column (timers.py:326-335, 593-597, 688-691). That is how claude-4, the live desktop account, gets keepalive turns.

Addition 'Identity binding': 'is disabled' holds only when the timer probe reports another account_key (timers.py:473-497). An attempt or admission-probe finding only sets identity_status (daemon.py:958-990). The lane is rejected either way.

Addition 'Per-job policy hash': 'Every job records the sha256 of the policy bytes it was evaluated under' is imprecise. The job row stores the daemon's hash at submission (daemon.py:1301), while each decision carries the evaluating daemon's hash (daemon.py:1026; scheduler.py:587). A job queued across a restart under a new policy is evaluated under the new one but keeps its old hash.

Test citations M-c8, Q-c7, Q-c29 and others use the `policy` fixture, which switches the reserve off (tests/unit/test_scheduler.py:21-27). They prove behaviour under the live policy, not under the shipped default, where an unmeasured Claude lane rejects Opus with reserve:fable:unmeasured (test_scheduler.py:412).

defect-0-4: 'claude-1, 6, 7 and 9 had two attempts from when they were measured' is a deduction from the one-slot rule, not an observation. '35 jobs waited with no open lane' should say that 34 of them were held behind-older-job and 1 no-slot (status admission.reasons).
verifier_missed: Gate peers bypass the chains and still use Fable. `subfleet gate plan|pr --peer` accepts only fable, astra or sol (subfleet/gate/cli.py:39), and sol only prints a note at 98-99. Each round submits a gate-review job with pinned_model=state['peer'] (subfleet/gate/round.py:58-68), so a gate can never use an Opus peer. Computed: gate-review attempts requested claude-fable-5-1 51 times (2026-09-22/23) and gpt-6-astra 55 times.

The reserve drove v2 promotions until it was removed. Computed over decisions JOIN attempts JOIN jobs (dispatch, no pinned model, tier standard, chosen astra): all 29 Opus-to-Astra promotions under policy hashes b600da62, a09458c6 and de99c319 (2026-09-19 to 2026-09-24) had at least one lane rejected reserve:fable:unmeasured. None of the 54 under 684b944f and 78e3b076 did. The shipped default still has the rule (default_policy.json:165-172; test_scheduler.py:412).

Timer reservations use admission capacity. Timer probe and keepalive holders are 'probe:timer:*' leases on lane:<id>:slot:0 (timers.py:325, 336-337), and _capacity_view counts every 'probe:%' lease as reserved_probes and marks that lane unavailable (daemon.py:892-893). A timer turn therefore counts against caps.max_active_attempts and blocks the lane's slot while it runs (scheduler.py:386, 456-459).

Model names hard-coded outside the policy: timer turns index policy['models']['haiku'] and ['terra'] (daemon.py:2604; timers.py:677), so a policy without those keys breaks the timers. The Claude adapter maps weekly-window scopes to fixed ids claude-fable-5-1, claude-opus-5-5 and claude-sonnet-5 (adapters/claude.py:85-93) whatever the policy's model ids.

Reset-credit overrides remove readings from routing. _pick drops the readings of any lane with a confirmed reset-credit override before evaluate (daemon.py:1017-1025), and enrich_view relabels them stale-provider and sets verdict admission-observed (timers.py:549-566). The shipped policy enables reset credits (default_policy.json:117-121) and the live policy disables them (live line 119).

A stale stored desktop flag also blocks re-enrolment. _enroll_lane_locked refuses to re-enrol a binding whose stored desktop column is set (daemon.py:645-646), so claude-1's credential could not be re-enrolled if that lane were ever disabled. The stored column changes only through enrolment, seeding or import, never from the view.

The pick path (PATH shim and `subfleet pick`) evaluates each model of the family as a read-only pin and never passes allow_desktop (picker.py:47-58). It also raises the headroom floor to max(policy floor, --min-headroom) (picker.py:53-55), so a shim-chosen Codex home obeys the same rejections as submission plus that floor.

claims.claim: The outcome classes are ok, limited, auth-dead, cli-too-old, content-filter, transient and unknown.

Claude limited signals: a rate_limit_event with status rejected (scope from rateLimitType via SCOPED_RATE_LIMITS, the requested model for errorCode credits_required, else account); credit wording (model scope, reason credits); limit wording such as 'usage-limit', 'session-limit', 'weekly-limit', 'limit-reached' (account scope, reason provider-limit).

Claude auth-dead signals: an organisation-block phrase anywhere in the corpus; an assistant or api_retry error kind of authentication_failed, oauth_org_not_allowed or account_on_hold; or a 401/unauthorized/token-revoked signature when no system/init event arrived. With system/init present the same signature is classed transient.
cli-too-old is Claude's first check (version-gate wording); Codex tests its OLD_CLI_RE after the success check.
content-filter is a Claude stop_reason of refusal on the result or any assistant message, and for Codex a failure event or stderr line matching content filter, trusted access or can't help/assist.

Claude transient signals are error kinds overloaded, server_error or rate_limit, TRANSIENT_RE (5xx, 429, overload, connection, timeouts, stream closed), or a truncated stream with no result; Codex transient is TRANSIENT_RE over failure events and stderr, including 5xx, 429, 401, DNS and TLS errors. Transient never writes a closure.
Codex auth-dead is AUTH_RE (incorrect API key, invalid_api_key, revoked refresh token, blocked organisation, 401 at the usage endpoint) over failure events and stderr, checked before success.

Codex limited is LIMIT_RE over failure events and stderr; the closure scope is an explicit non-'model' scope field, else a model id, else account; the clock is reported when the event or text gives one, else now + 3600 s guessed; the reason is credits when CREDITS_RE matches.
A limit without a reported clock closes until now + 3600 s with clock_source guessed; a reported clock is kept even if already past.
The store keeps one open closure per lane and scope and extends it only to a later until_at.
The scheduler refuses a lane for a model while an open future closure exists on that lane at account scope or at that model's id.

Finalization retries when the job is not cancelled, seq < max_attempts, and the attempt was lost on a read-only job, or limited with no pinned lane, or transient unless the job is lane-pinned and already had a transient on that lane.

auth-dead, cli-too-old, content-filter and unknown attempts are not retried at finalization; a final limited, auth-dead or cli-too-old attempt gives job rc 4, 5 or 6, a lost job 125, a cancelled job 130.
An auth-dead attempt sets its lane enabled=0 and records the auth-dead lane with the timers.
An attempt that never launched (reserved-no-launch, starting-no-receipt) is recorded unknown and the job is requeued while seq < max_attempts.

On retry, a limited attempt's lane (and its re-enrolled successor) is excluded for the job; a lane with two transients is excluded; after a first transient the retry is pinned once to the same lane and model if that pair is routable, and routes as submitted if the lane refuses it for anything but a full slot.

An unpinned job's candidate models are its task chain from its tier upward, and the first model with a candidate lane wins; a -m job's chain is that one model; a lane pin keeps only the chain's first model.
A retrying job is set to state waiting, wait_reason capacity, with next_check_at now + 60 s after a transient and now after other classes.
The daemon writes wait_reason values capacity, route, workspace and uncertain; the WaitReason enum also lists dependency and approval, which no code writes, and omits route.
