additions.name: Daemon-side acceptance overrides and explicit non-acceptance notice
additions.description: After the adapter classifies an attempt, the daemon demotes `ok` to `unknown` when the daemon itself signalled the attempt or the deliverable is empty, and keeps the adapter's verdict in evidence. A terminal notice names a kept-but-unaccepted deliverable and says that `-o` was not written.

additions.name: Export after acceptance
additions.description: `-o` is an export of the accepted attempt's deliverable. The job must hold the out:<path> lease, the sha256 is checked, and the file is written atomically. A replay cannot overwrite a newer owner's output.

additions.name: Per-attempt served-model attestation for both providers
additions.description: Claude attests from its own transcript range and ignores only exact-shape synthetic API-error frames. Codex attests from the thread's rollout. The result is stored as attempts.attestation and model_served.

additions.name: Shared closure ledger with reported or guessed clocks
additions.description: A limit writes a closure row (reason provider-limit or credits, clock reported or guessed) that every later routing decision reads. The row is scoped to the account or to one model.

additions.name: Transient retry pin and lane exclusion
additions.description: After a first transient, the job retries once on the same lane and model after 60 s. A second transient, or any limit, excludes that lane for the job.

additions.name: Job-level wall clock across attempts
additions.description: max_wall_s runs from the first reservation and cancels waiting and running jobs alike.

additions.name: Outcome-to-exit-code table
additions.description: A final limited, auth-dead or cli-too-old attempt gives job rc 4, 5 or 6; lost gives 125 and cancelled gives 130. The raw provider rc stays on the attempt.

additions.name: Quarantine on unverified containment
additions.description: When processes outlive the exit receipt or a kill, the attempt is quarantined instead of finalized. `kill --confirm-dead` or `--force-release` resolves it, and the only record it adds is salvage.

additions.name: Gate verdict schema and positive attestation
additions.description: Gate verdicts are the one output with a schema: a strict sentinel JSON object bound to the artifact revision. The peer round must be positively attested for Claude, and a mismatch is refused for any provider.

verifier_cell_problems: Failure handling cell: 'Each attempt gets one of seven classes' overreaches. A quarantined or guardian-lost attempt gets no class: the store has 42 quarantined and 3 lost attempts with a NULL outcome_class (daemon.py:4469-4478, 4671-4673).

Failure handling cell: 'A retry excludes the limited lane and walks the task chain upward' misdescribes routing. Each retry re-routes from the job's own tier, and the same model on another open lane wins before any higher model (scheduler.py:339-343, 550-585). Opus went to Astra in FH-c24 only because no Opus lane was admissible.

Failure handling cell: 'A process still alive after exit ends the job lost' is too narrow. An unverifiable census (a ps enumeration error with no live pid) also ends the job lost, and it caused 26 of the 36 retained cases (procs.py:444-445, 462-463).
Failure handling cell: '(3; 1 for gate rounds)' leaves out conversation turns and session revives, which also submit max_attempts=1 (conversations/service.py:1794; sessions/revive.py:320).

Output contract cell: 'The daemon turns ok into unknown when it signalled the attempt or the deliverable is empty' omits the turn-job exemption (daemon.py:4699, 4716). 'only gates refuse it' should say that accepted Claude turns carry mismatches: 4 in the store, all '<synthetic>'.

Budget cell: 'The admission pass cancels a waiting job that is past it' hides how. It calls kill (daemon.py:3247-3249 -> 2334-2356), which also cancels non-independent child jobs, records job.cancel_requested with no job.wall_limit event, and writes the notice 'cancelled before launch' even when an attempt already ran.
Budget cell: 'the job ends cancelled with rc 130' needs the turn exemption: a completed turn is accepted despite a stop (daemon.py:4745-4748).
Budget cell: 'Seven wall-limit kills were recorded' counts only kills of running attempts. Three more waiting jobs were cancelled 6 h or more after started_at with no wall event (see missed).
Budget cell: 'a lane is refused when any fresh window is at 85% or more' should say that only readings at account scope or at the requested model's id count (scheduler.py:419-422).

Addition 'Quarantine on unverified containment': 'the only record it adds is salvage' overreaches. Resolution also changes the attempt state to interrupted or lost, deletes leases and records a quarantine.confirmed_dead or quarantine.force_release event. Salvage is taken only when the census is verified empty, and a turn gets end trees instead (daemon.py:4480-4503).

Addition 'Transient retry pin and lane exclusion': 'retries once on the same lane and model after 60 s' holds only while that pair is routable and the lane refuses it for nothing but a full slot. Otherwise the job routes as submitted (daemon.py:1071-1073, 1078-1096, 3361-3375).
Defect 'Claude classifier treats the worker's own words': 'Documents and reviews about subfleet itself are the likeliest trigger' has no evidence. The one observed case is a handoff report.

Defect 'A run that exits 0 is reported lost': 'when any process outlives its exit receipt by 3 s' and 'The census does not record which processes lingered' are contradicted by procs.py:322-352 and by the stored quarantine_reason JSON.
Defect '4 MB stream' evidence says 'tests/unit/test_claude_large_stream.py (exists; not run)'. It was run this session and passed (5 tests).
verifier_missed: Wall-clock cancels of waiting jobs are indistinguishable from operator kills. The admission pass calls self.kill (daemon.py:3247-3249), which records job.cancel_requested and writes the notice 'cancelled before launch' (daemon.py:2342-2356), not job.wall_limit. Computed: 3 retained jobs (20260927-091948-wt-archive-review-opus, 20260927-090026-ccbw217r4-review-opus, 20260927-081407-probe-load-review-opus) each had a transient a1, were cancelled 6 h or more after started_at with rc 130, and got the notice 'cancelled before launch'. So wall-clock cancellations number at least 10, not 7.

Most 'writers remain after exit receipt' quarantines are census failures, not lingering processes. Containment is unverifiable whenever a ps read fails (procs.py:404-410, 427-445, 462-463). Computed: 25 of 36 had only 'marker enumeration unavailable', 1 had all three enumeration errors, and only 10 recorded live pids. 23 of the 36 had provider rc 0 and so lost a finished deliverable (no classification, acceptance or export).

The 4 MB truncation hit the handoff job twice. 20260920-161631-handoff-microcosm-us-release/a2 exited 0 with a success result at byte 4,614,213 of a 4,622,117-byte stream and was classed transient. Its a1 had been classed limited from its text, and only a3 was a genuine rate_limit_event rejection. Under current code both a1 and a2 reclassify as limited from deliverable text (computed, ofb-verify/reclassify2.py), so the job would still fail with rc 4.

Auth checks run before success on non-text frames too. An api_retry frame with error authentication_failed that the CLI recovered from makes an otherwise successful run auth-dead (claude.py:1554-1561 over claude_stream.py:243-247), and that disables the lane (daemon.py:4769-4771). This was computed with a constructed frame shaped per claude_stream.py:27-28, 429-437; it has not been observed in the store. An api_retry with error overloaded followed by success stays ok.

Lane disabling leaves no reason on the lane row. The lanes table has no reason column (store_schema.sql lanes). update_lane(enabled=0) is called for an auth-dead attempt (daemon.py:4769-4771), an auth-dead probe (2923-2925), a timer probe auth-dead or identity-mismatch (timers.py:495-497), an auth-dead keepalive (672-675), a non-canonical duplicate (310-316) and an open auth-dead closure (301-306). The reason survives only in timer.verdict or timer.probe events and in-memory timer metadata (timers.py:284-287). No code path re-enables a lane (grep enabled=1/True finds only timers.py:535).

The rc table has two more rows. An attempt that never launched and is not retried ends the job failed with rc 1 (daemon.py:4400-4403). A guardian lost without an exit receipt goes through _finalize(lost=True): rc 125, class unknown, with a retry only for read-only jobs (daemon.py:4501-4502, 4665-4673, 4751-4753).

The same text-before-success ordering reaches credit wording: a successful run whose text says 'out-of-extra-usage' or 'monthly-spend-limit' is classed limited with a model-scope credits closure, which blocks that model on the lane (claude.py:1602-1627; computed with probe2.py).
open_questions: Step 5 dispatches reviewers with `subfleet run --task review --tier standard`, which routes to claude-opus-5-5. A review of this document will very likely quote phrases such as 'session-limit' or 'usage-limit', and the current Claude classifier would then class a successful review as limited, withhold its -o, and close that lane for about an hour (defect 1). Options: tell reviewers not to use those literal phrases, route the review to Codex with --tier hard, or check each review's attempt for class limited with rc 0 before trusting a missing output.

The 36 lost-after-exit-receipt jobs: the containment census records pids and process shapes but not command lines, so it is undetermined whether the survivors were worker-started background processes, provider helpers or something else.
Why the wall-limit event for 20260927-043608-pr1011-puf982-v2 fired 1,417 s after its due time was not determined; the other six fired within 101 s.

Whether conversation-turn attempts are meant to attest the whole conversation transcript (launch notes transcript_offset 0) or only the turn's own range was not checked against the conversations launch code (subfleet/conversations/launch.py, claude_turn.py).

Defect 4 cell: 'which removes the reserve rather than fixing how it is measured' is a judgement, not a mechanism claim. verifier_missed: An unverifiable census counts as not contained: Containment.verified_empty requires no inspection errors (subfleet/procs.py:339-340, 462-463). After an exit receipt, a failed `ps -axEww` marker read therefore quarantines the attempt and loses the job (subfleet/daemon.py:4635-4645). Resolving a quarantine does not rescue the job. _resolve_quarantine re-runs containment. With --confirm-dead and a census that is still not empty, it only records quarantine.still_live. Otherwise it deletes all of the job's and attempt's leases, salvages a writable non-turn job only when the census is verified empty, and sets the attempt to lost or interrupted. The job row stays lost or cancelled with no accepted_attempt_id, so -o is never written (subfleet/daemon.py:4480-4501). Computed: 4 quarantine.confirmed_dead events and 0 force_release in the store.

A quarantined job has more effects than out: leases. It refuses in-place writable submits into the same checkout (subfleet/daemon.py:1766-1771) and refuses `resume` of the job (subfleet/daemon.py:1502-1505). It blocks lane re-enrollment (subfleet/daemon.py:659-661, 702-704), `login codex` (subfleet/operations.py:118-121) and lane transfer (subfleet/lanes_transfer.py:88). It also pins the job against retention pruning (subfleet/retention.py:99).

additions.name: Segment-scoped attached-launch guard
additions.description: `subfleet hook PreToolUse` checks each Bash command with a shlex tokenizer. It ignores heredoc bodies and splits the command into shell segments. It honours SUBFLEET_ATTACHED_OK=1 and -d only inside the offending segment, and it denies with a PreToolUse permissionDecision rather than v1's decision block. `daemon install --hooks` writes the entry with a 5 s timeout, and that entry was installed live on 2026-09-27.

additions.name: Direct provider verbs refused at the CLI
additions.description: `subfleet codex` and `subfleet claude` are refused before argument parsing, with a reason naming the ledger, lane accounting and cancellation tree. The v1 wrappers `codex-run` and `claude-lane` therefore fail instead of launching.

additions.name: Codex never-rules overlay preflight
additions.description: Before each Codex launch the daemon checks the operator-staged never-rules hook. The hook bytes must match TRUST's SHA-256, the Codex version must match the pinned one, and an app-server hooks/list probe must report the hook enabled and trusted. The daemon fails closed with code 7, and it caches a verified verdict for 30 days keyed on version, home, override and seed files.

additions.name: Per-attempt served-model attestation
additions.description: Every attempt stores attested, mismatch or unattested, along with the served model. Claude attestation never gives a false positive, and it ignores synthetic API-error frames. A gate discards mismatch rounds for any peer and unattested Claude rounds, and a completion notice names a non-attested status. The status does not change whether an ordinary job succeeds.

additions.name: Daemon-owned native resume
additions.description: `subfleet resume` (alias `resume-codex`) submits a job pinned to the source lane, carrying the source's native session id. The daemon then continues that session with the adapter's resume_launch instead of starting a fresh one.

additions.name: Retention and decision-row dedup
additions.description: An hourly retention timer prunes the oldest unpinned terminal jobs, with their notices, decisions, attempts, artifacts and readings. Detached jobs are held to 500 jobs and 2 GiB, turn jobs to 2,000, 4 GiB and 14 days. The timer also removes acknowledged or surfaced service notices after 14 days. A repeated wait with an unchanged verdict writes no decision row. The events table has no retention.

additions.name: Kill containment with quarantine
additions.description: An operator kill or a wall-limit stop sends SIGTERM to the process group, waits up to 15 s for a verified-empty census, then sends SIGKILL to the group and owned pids and settles for up to 3 s. If containment cannot be verified, the attempt is quarantined rather than marked finished.

verifier_cell_problems: Defect v1_item 10 (kill), status 'still-present': the v1 item was README drift (the README said SIGTERM only while the code escalated). The v2 README.md has no kill, SIGTERM or SIGKILL text (grep -in 'sigterm|sigkill|kill' README.md finds nothing relevant), so the drift is gone. The status should be superseded or fixed, not still-present. The text also overstates by saying the daemon 'then sends SIGKILL'. SIGKILL is sent only when the census is not verified empty after the 15 s grace (subfleet/daemon.py:4435-4441).

Defect v1_item 10 (nudge cooldown), status 'still-present': the v1 defect was the README saying 10 minutes. The v2 README has no cooldown text (grep -in cooldown README.md: none), so there is no drift left to be present. 90 s is simply the v2 value. The status should be superseded.

Defect v1_item 7 (superseded drift pin) says the overlay must match TRUST 'before any Codex launch'. Isolated-review Codex launches skip the preflight (`None if spec.isolated_review`, subfleet/daemon.py:3998-3999). Same overreach in the addition 'Codex never-rules overlay preflight' ('Before each Codex launch').

Defect v1_item 7 (bash -c, still-present): 'The function's docstring makes this a stated limit'. The docstring says only 'Indirect launches through scripts remain the caller's responsibility' (subfleet/hooks.py:612-613). It does not name bash -c or eval.
Defect v1_item 0 'More attached launches pass the guard' is incomplete and understates the gap; see missed items (comment-merged lines, shell keywords, env options, shlex fail-open).
Defect v1_item 11: 'only tests import' policy.pick. tools/compare_decisions.py:60 also imports it.
Defect v1_item 10 (notify states) cites subfleet/contracts.py:100-104. NoticeState is at contracts.py:102-106.

Defect v1_item 9 (third entry): 'Retention is per job, so a retained job keeps every row' does not say why the storm job is retained. It has a pending completion notice addressed to a session, and retention pins every such job (subfleet/retention.py:103-104). Computed: SELECT state FROM notices WHERE job_id='20260920-154810-guard-preflight-codex-proof' -> pending. 120 terminal detached jobs are pinned this way, so the 273 MB of decision rows stays until someone acknowledges that notice.

Defect v1_item 0 (timer alerts): 'no code reads the operator session's notices' should be scoped to the v2 tree. A grep of subfleet/, app/, tools/ and bin/ for the literal "operator" as a session finds only the fallback at subfleet/daemon.py:1989. Code outside v2 was not checked.

Addition 'Per-attempt served-model attestation': 'Claude attestation never gives a false positive' restates the docstring's design intent (subfleet/adapters/claude.py:1794-1795); it is not a verified property. The filter drops only API-error frames with the exact sentinel and zero usage (subfleet/adapters/claude_stream.py:74-96). The store holds 4 succeeded conversation turns (latest 2026-09-27T23:43Z) recorded as mismatch with served model '<synthetic>'.

Addition 'Retention and decision-row dedup': 'turn jobs to 2,000, 4 GiB and 14 days' reads as a 14-day maximum. 14 days is a minimum keep after a turn ends (subfleet/contracts.py:250-254, subfleet/retention.py:96-97). The phrase 'prunes the oldest unpinned terminal jobs' also omits what pins a job: non-terminal jobs and gate reviews, jobs with a pending or offered session notice, jobs with salvage artifacts the daemon cannot prove landed (the daemon passes no salvage_referenced_elsewhere), parents, and lease holders (retention.py:89-115; daemon.py:2507-2511). As a result the detached pool held 532 terminal jobs on 2026-09-28 against a 500 budget (computed).

Addition 'Kill containment with quarantine': SIGKILL is conditional on the census not being verified empty (daemon.py:4435). For turn jobs, conversations.stop runs before containment (daemon.py:4164-4166).

Defect v1_item 8 (partly-fixed) says 'where v1 enforced this for Fable peers only'. That is a comparison with the retired tree, sourced from the old doc, not from code read this session. Label it as such or cut it.
verifier_missed: The attached-launch guard fails open whenever shlex cannot tokenize the command: `except ValueError: return None` (subfleet/hooks.py:629-632). Computed: attached_runner("echo $'it\\'s'; codex exec x") -> None, a valid bash command in which the ANSI-C quote confuses posix shlex.

A trailing comment on one line swallows the newline that should end the segment, so the next line joins it. shlex's default '#' commenter consumes the newline. Computed: attached_runner('cd /tmp # go\ncodex exec x') -> None, with tokens ['cd','/tmp','codex','exec','x'], while '# note\ncodex exec x' is denied.

Shell grouping and keywords are not stripped before the command word, so attached_runner returns None for all of these (computed): '{ codex exec x; }', 'if true; then codex exec x; fi', 'while true; do codex exec x; done', '! codex exec x'. env options are not skipped either, since only '--' is skipped after a wrapper (hooks.py:650-653), so 'env -i codex exec x' -> None. The same holds for 'stdbuf -oL codex exec x', 'caffeinate codex exec x' and 'codex --full-auto exec x'.

The distribution allowlist is test-enforced: tests/unit/test_guard_overlay.py:163-167 asserts the wheel packages only 'subfleet' and the sdist includes only /subfleet, /README.md, /pyproject.toml and /uv.lock. bin/codex is therefore excluded by design. No v2 code installs the shim: grep of subfleet/ and tools/ for 'codex-shim|bin/codex|PATH shim' finds only docstrings at subfleet/picker.py:1 and subfleet/cli.py:499.

doctor's never-rules row (subfleet/doctor.py:349-367) passes when any PreToolUse command in ~/.claude/settings.json contains 'never-rules', 'never_rules' or 'subfleet-guard'. It checks presence by name only and does not compare the Claude hook with the Codex overlay, so the pattern-kill, axiom-brief-regime and hand-authored-rulespec drift is invisible to doctor.

v2 turns a limited outcome into a closure: `if outcome.closure: self.store.add_closure(outcome.closure)` (subfleet/daemon.py:4775-4776). capacity.build_view feeds active closures into lane eligibility (subfleet/capacity.py:366-406), and pick skips lanes with open closures (subfleet/picker.py:94). This is v2's replacement for v1's 'a hard-limit observation does not upgrade window confidence' (v1 item 10) and bears on v1 item 5.

Supporting computation for the decision-row fix (v1 item 9). By evaluation day: 2026-09-20 had 6,832 rows and 2026-09-21 had 25,917, both dominated by one job. From 2026-09-22 through 2026-09-27 it was 81-297 rows a day, and no job wrote more than 8 rows after 2026-09-23. Query: SELECT substr(evaluated_at,1,10),count(*) FROM decisions GROUP BY 1, and per-job counts WHERE evaluated_at>='2026-09-23'.

Retention pins every job that has a pending or offered notice addressed to a non-empty session (subfleet/retention.py:103-104). A job whose dispatching session never returns is therefore never pruned. 120 terminal detached jobs are pinned this way, the 28,022-row storm job among them (computed). Retention.py:113-115 also pins any job with a salvage artifact not proven landed, and the daemon never passes salvage_referenced_elsewhere (daemon.py:2507-2511); 231 jobs have salvage artifacts. Result: 532 terminal detached jobs against RETENTION_MAX_JOBS 500 (contracts.py:248), with the oldest, finished 2026-09-19T16:00:47Z, still present.

store.acknowledge_notices (subfleet/store.py:663-669) has no caller in subfleet/, so `runs show` via cli.py:1511-1530 is the only acknowledgement path. Nothing, CLI or daemon, acknowledges a service notice (negative id) except a direct notice.ack op call.

The PostToolUse asyncRewake path delivers only job notices: it filters _pending rows by job_id (subfleet/hooks.py:585-603). Service-notice re-injection is therefore confined to SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit, and a Subfleet-launched process sees only job-named rows (hooks.py:438-439).

Should bin/codex ship in the release, or should the ~/bin/codex symlink be removed? pyproject.toml excludes bin/, and the symlink has dangled since the 2026-09-22T13:31Z release.
Where should timer alerts go? alerts.operator_session is unset in both policies, so 1,046 alerts sit pending on the literal session 'operator'.

The auth-dead path disables a lane with update_lane(enabled=0) (subfleet/daemon.py:2924, 4770) and calls timers.record_auth_dead. I did not read what record_auth_dead stores, so I cannot say whether it accounts for the 7 Claude lanes reported disabled with no recorded reason.

There are 578 non-turn jobs against a detached budget of 500, yet job 20260920-154810-guard-preflight-codex-proof (28,022 decision rows) survives. I did not trace retention._pins to see why it is protected.

The 4 succeeded 'mismatch' attempts are conversation turns attested by subfleet/conversations/classify.py, which I did not read. Whether its synthetic-frame filter differs from adapters/claude_stream.is_synthetic_api_error is unverified.

claims.claim: The daemon is installed as the launchd agent com.subfleet.daemon with RunAtLoad and KeepAlive and ProcessType Interactive. The live agent runs subfleetd with --state-root ~/.subfleet as pid 61062.
claims.evidence: subfleet/cli.py:2369-2392 (_plist); observed: `launchctl list | awk '/com.subfleet.daemon/'` -> `61062 0 com.subfleet.daemon`; `plutil -extract ProgramArguments json -o - ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.subfleet.daemon.plist`; `plutil -extract ProcessType raw …` -> Interactive

claims.claim: The caller's `subfleet run` only talks to the daemon over the AF_UNIX socket <state root>/daemon.sock. Inside a Claude session it defaults to detached and returns once the daemon has the job; outside a session it blocks.
claims.checked: subfleet/client.py:52, 276-293, 359; subfleet/cli.py:138-161 (launch_mode), 534-549 and 578-582 (stage_prompt), 798-840 (cmd_run)
claims.correction: `subfleet run` submits over the AF_UNIX socket <state root>/daemon.sock (client.py:52, 292-293, 359), but it is not the only thing it does: inline prompt text is first written to <state root>/inbox (cli.py:534-549, 578-582). Inside a Claude session launch_mode returns 'detached' (cli.py:157-160) and cmd_run returns right after the submit reply (cli.py:836-839), except that `--attach` makes it wait inline (cli.py:158-159, 802, 840). `-d` and SUBFLEET_RUN_DETACH override the default either way (cli.py:150-156). Outside a session it blocks in wait_jobs (cli.py:161, 840).

claims.claim: For each attempt the daemon spawns `sys.executable -m subfleet.guardian --attempt-dir … --cwd … --stdout-path … --stderr-path … --launch-fd N [--stdin-path …] -- <provider argv>`. The spawn uses stdin, stdout and stderr on /dev/null, close_fds, only the gate fd passed, and cwd set to the package root.

The guardian calls os.setsid() and ignores SIGTERM and SIGINT. It then reads one byte from the launch fd, and any value other than b"1" (including EOF after a daemon crash) returns 127 without spawning a provider.

Before writing the release byte, the daemon records guardian_pid, pgid (equal to the guardian pid), boot_id and proc_start on the attempt row with state 'starting'. If identity cannot be read within about 2 s, the daemon closes the gate and records guardian-identity-unavailable.
boot_id is kern.bootsessionuuid, falling back to kern.boottime, and proc_start is `ps -o lstart=`. Liveness is 'alive' only when start time and boot id match, and 'unknown' when inspection fails.

The guardian publishes start.json (guardian_pid, pgid, boot_id, proc_start, started_at) before it spawns the provider. It then runs the provider with stdin from the prompt file and stdout/stderr in 0600 files, and writes exit.json (rc, signal, finished_at, wall_s, child_pid, spawn_error) after wait.
The provider argv is prefixed with `/usr/sbin/taskpolicy -c utility` unless SUBFLEET_PROVIDER_QOS=inherit is set or taskpolicy is absent.

The daemon adds SUBFLEET_JOB, SUBFLEET_ATTEMPT and SUBFLEET_ROOT to the guardian environment. Containment counts the process group, the descendants of the guardian and child, and processes whose environment carries those markers (via `ps -axEww`). Signals go only to a recorded group leader whose identity still matches.
claims.checked: subfleet/daemon.py:4050; subfleet/procs.py:384-463 (markers 426-444), 466-477 (signal_group), 480-490 (signal_process); subfleet/daemon.py:4288, 4428-4441
claims.correction: The daemon adds SUBFLEET_JOB, SUBFLEET_ATTEMPT and SUBFLEET_ROOT (daemon.py:4050). additions.name: Launch gate with durable guardian identity
additions.description: The provider cannot start until the daemon has committed the guardian's pid, pgid, boot id and start time. The guardian blocks on a pipe byte the daemon writes only after that commit, so a daemon crash in between leaves no unrecorded provider.

additions.name: Provider QoS clamp
additions.description: Each provider and its descendants run under `taskpolicy -c utility` while the daemon runs at Interactive, so agent work stays below the operator's apps. SUBFLEET_PROVIDER_QOS=inherit opts out.

additions.name: Per-job detached worktrees
additions.description: A writable job that is not in place gets `git worktree add --detach` at the caller's HEAD under $SUBFLEET_HOME/worktrees/<job id>. The prompt gets a note naming the worktree, and Claude starts at the caller's relative prefix. The worktree is removed only by retention.

additions.name: Salvage refs as the return path
additions.description: Worker changes come back as a commit under refs/subfleet-salvage/, parented on the baseline, with the caller's HEAD, index and files untouched. A retry is told the checkpoint and the refs to continue from.

additions.name: Write-target leases and writer caps
additions.description: The leases `worktree:<git toplevel>` and `out:<path>` serialize or refuse writers that would collide. One session holds at most 8 live writable jobs, and a second live instance of a session cannot add writers.

additions.name: Write preamble and --no-preamble
additions.description: Writable prompts are prefixed with a fixed instruction block (workspace only, commit steps, never push to main or master). `--no-preamble` removes that block but keeps the workspace note.

additions.name: /tmp workdir refusal
additions.description: A -C directory under /tmp or /private/tmp is refused unless --allow-tmp is passed, by both the CLI and the daemon.

additions.name: Headless block on Claude prompts
additions.description: Every Claude attempt's stdin prompt begins with a block forbidding background tasks and wait-for-notification patterns, unless the prompt already carries the marker.

additions.name: Isolated-review hardening
additions.description: For -I review jobs, Claude drops web tools and gets --add-dir for the review root. Codex first inspects its config layers and MCP inventory through `codex app-server` and `codex mcp list`, then launches ephemeral with user config, rules, project docs, 17 features and every MCP server disabled.

additions.name: Attended conversation turns on the same guardian
additions.description: The same guardian also hosts attended conversation turns. The provider's stdin becomes a pipe fed through a Unix control socket that accepts only the daemon's peer. The observed turn argv uses `--input-format stream-json` and `--permission-prompt-tool stdio`.

verifier_cell_problems: Worker cell: 'It then runs the provider under taskpolicy -c utility and writes start.json and exit.json (guardian.py:152-204)': start.json is published before the provider is spawned (guardian.py:151), which is outside the cited range. Only exit.json follows the wait.

Worker cell: 'inside a session, returns once the daemon has accepted it': not with --attach, which waits inline inside a session (cli.py:158-159, 802, 840). -d and SUBFLEET_RUN_DETACH also override the default (cli.py:150-156).

Worker change_from_v1: 'Claude output moved from --output-format json to stream-json with a session id chosen before launch'. v1 also passed --session-id "$SID" (v1's launch line as read by tests/unit/test_claude_v1_parity.py:104-115; claude.py:2011-2017). The only change is json to stream-json plus --verbose.
Worker change_from_v1: 'In v1 the CLI started one runner process per call with nohup and a new session, and the runner's EXIT trap closed the ledger entry' cites nothing in this draft.

Worker context cell: 'Read-only Claude gets plan mode, a Read/Glob/Grep tool list…'. Non-isolated read-only jobs also get WebSearch and WebFetch, plus --no-chrome (claude.py:116, 1214-1221). Only isolated reviews are limited to Read,Glob,Grep (claude.py:115, 1214, 1226-1227).

Worker context cell: 'Changes come back as a commit under refs/subfleet-salvage/, never merged or pushed'. Subfleet code never pushes, but the worker can. Writable Claude runs with --dangerously-skip-permissions and the network, and writable Codex gets network_access=true under both the shipped and the live policy; the adapter comment says 'gh, curl and git push reach the network' (codex.py:453-459; default_policy.json:63-65). The preamble forbids only pushing to main or master (daemon.py:192-197). A snapshot is also made only when the tree changed (salvage.py:289-290), and the worker's own commits are not ancestors of the salvage ref (salvage.py:299-300).

Worker context cell: 'Codex gets the lane's CODEX_HOME, --sandbox and a never-rules hook'. Isolated reviews get no hook and set features.hooks=false (codex.py:466; isolation.py:20). The cell reports Claude's global CLAUDE.md, hooks and skills loading but says nothing on Codex. A non-isolated Codex launch passes no flag that ignores the lane home's config or the repository's project docs (codex.py:433-467).

Worker context cell: 'all 115 writable … none of the 73 read-only' is time-bound. A re-run at about 2026-09-28T00:45Z gives 117 writable (122 launches) and still 73 read-only, with 6 without a transcript.

Worker context change_from_v1: 'refuses a second in-place writer in one checkout' is narrower than the code. An --in-place job is refused when any live writable job, worktree jobs included, was submitted with the same -C workdir (daemon.py:1766-1768, 1782-1786), or when a live job records or holds that toplevel (1666-1680). Every writable job also takes a `worktree:` lease at admission (3563).
Worker context change_from_v1: 'v1 created no worktree, so concurrent runs aimed at one directory shared it' cites nothing in this draft.

Additions, 'Provider QoS clamp': 'so agent work stays below the operator's apps' is an effect claim resting on code comments (cli.py:2381-2388; guardian.py:18-24) and a docs/reports file. It was not measured this session.

Additions, 'Per-job detached worktrees': 'The worktree is removed only by retention' is wrong. Admission also discards it on a route refusal (daemon.py:3828-3839, 3871) and on a failed or timed-out `worktree add` (2653-2670).

Additions, 'Salvage refs as the return path': 'Worker changes come back as a commit … parented on the baseline' omits two things. No snapshot is made when the tree is unchanged, and intermediate worker commits are dropped from the ref's history; only the final tree survives (salvage.py:289-300; daemon.py:4544-4550).

defect v1 item 2, status 'fixed': overstated. -s workspace-write overrides the build-only policy map (cli.py:658; daemon.py:1203-1205). 141 writable review and 52 writable research dispatch jobs are retained, and 105 of 314 writable dispatch jobs ran --in-place in the caller's checkout (computed).
verifier_missed: Worker environment is the launchd daemon's, not the caller's. The plist sets only PATH (captured at `daemon install`) and SUBFLEET_HOME (cli.py:2374-2375; observed plist EnvironmentVariables keys ['PATH','SUBFLEET_HOME']). The guardian inherits the daemon's env plus env_add, minus env_remove (daemon.py:4046-4054). The caller session's venv, exported tokens and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR never reach the worker. The daemon PATH resolves the same claude 2.1.280 binary as the shell (observed).

Claude worker transcripts go to the operator's own ~/.claude/projects, keyed by the worktree path. Keychain-token lanes inject no CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (credentials.py:39-50), and the transcript path defaults to ~/.claude/projects/<encoded workdir>/<session>.jsonl (claude.py:1230-1248). Worker sessions therefore sit in the same history as interactive ones; the transcript_path values in launch.json notes confirm this.

Salvage records only the final tree. The snapshot's parent is the attempt's reservation baseline (salvage.py:282-300; daemon.py:4544-4548), so commits the worker made during the attempt are not ancestors of the ref. The worktree HEAD is kept only as `checkpoint` in salvage.json (daemon.py:4549-4550). A retry's baseline is the worktree HEAD at re-admission (daemon.py:2674, 3594). No snapshot is made when the tree is unchanged (salvage.py:289-290). For an in-place job the baseline tree includes the caller's pre-existing dirty files, so only the delta is captured (daemon.py:2676-2677; salvage.py:269-272).

Worktrees are cut on the first admission pass, before routing and capacity. _workspace runs at daemon.py:3325, ahead of the capacity hold at 3492-3520, so a writable job waiting for capacity already has its worktree while jobs.worktree stays NULL. One live waiting job has this state (computed). Every admission transaction is recorded as an 'attempt.reserved' event, holds included (daemon.py:3457, 3514), so event counts are not attempt counts; one orphan job has about 290 such events and no attempt.

Retention prunes every unpinned terminal job on each pass. Job size includes the worktree (retention.py:277-281), and the salvage-pinned worktrees (84G) keep the detached pool above its 2 GiB budget forever. The prune loop, oldest first, runs until budgets are met and skips only protected jobs (retention.py:299-317), deleting their jobs, attempts, notices, decisions and artifacts rows and the job directory (retention.py:350-387). Result: 1,375 jobs pruned since 2026-09-19 while 606 are retained (computed from events). The 500-job cap is never the binding limit, and job evidence without a pin is deleted at the next pass.

Policy picks the sandbox only when -s is omitted (cli.py:658; daemon.py:1203-1205, 1469-1477). An isolated review or gate round is always read-only (1473-1474), and a -m pin without --task falls to the '*' entry, read-only. The retained store holds 141 writable review and 52 writable research dispatch jobs, and 105 of 314 writable dispatch jobs ran --in-place (computed).

Kill path: SIGTERM to the recorded group, then SIGKILL to the group after term_grace_s if the census is not empty, then SIGKILL to each recorded survivor. Every signal is gated on a still-matching identity (daemon.py:4428-4441; procs.py:466-490). The guardian ignores SIGTERM and SIGINT so that it can be rechecked before escalation (guardian.py:117-120).

Codex lane homes are re-validated at launch, and a home whose auth.json holds OPENAI_API_KEY or an api_key auth_mode is refused (daemon.py:1788-1799, 3995). Isolated Claude reviews are refused when the environment carries managed-settings variables (isolation.py:15-16, 32-40; cli.py:597-603).

WRITE_PREAMBLE tells the worker to 'Commit each coherent step on the assigned branch' (daemon.py:195), but a worker that is not in place is given a detached worktree with no branch (daemon.py:2663; tests/fake/test_main_refusal_write_dir.py:27 asserts detached HEAD). The instruction names a branch that does not exist.
open_questions: Does `subfleet runs show` or `subfleet wait` print a job's salvage ref? Not checked: `runs show` acknowledges notices and was off limits, and the notice itself does not name the ref.
Which `claude` binary and version does the daemon's plist PATH resolve? The 2.1.280 --help text was read from this session's shell PATH.

Which AGENTS.md and project instructions does a normal Codex worker load? That is Codex's own behavior. Subfleet passes no suppressing flag, but loading was not observed in a Codex rollout this session.

The 6 orphan worktree jobs show many 'attempt.reserved' event rows with no attempt_id and no surviving attempt. Are these rolled-back reservations, and do they confirm the cancel-before-attempt path for the leak?
How much of the 78 GB in ~/.subfleet/worktrees belongs to salvage-pinned jobs versus live or unpinned ones was not computed.

new_features: Nested workflow(nameOrRef, args): runs a saved workflow or a {scriptPath} script inline as a sub-step. Nesting is one level only (workflow() inside a child throws). The child shares the parent's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal and token budget, and its agents show under a group named for the child. Separately, sub-agents.md lists the Workflow tool as unavailable to subagents, so a worker cannot launch a workflow through the tool. Source: bundled /workflow-authoring skill (2.1.280); sub-agents.md tool filter list.

Per-agent options beyond model: effort ('low' through 'max'); isolation:'worktree', which runs the agent in a fresh git worktree (about 200-500 ms setup, removed automatically if unchanged) and is meant for agents that edit files in parallel; agentType, which uses a custom subagent type and composes with schema; plus phase and label. The public page only hints at isolation through an example prompt about each file getting its own isolated copy. Source: bundled /workflow-authoring skill; workflows.md 'Migrate many files in parallel'.

budget is a hard ceiling with a shared pool: {total, spent(), remaining()} comes from a '+500k' turn directive, counts output tokens across the main loop and every workflow, and agent() throws once it is exhausted. Source: bundled /workflow-authoring skill.

Saved workflows: /workflows then `s` saves a run's script. The project location (.claude/workflows/) uses the closest existing directory in a monorepo, and every one along the path loads. The personal location is ~/.claude/workflows/ (or under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR). A saved workflow runs as /<name>, and a project copy wins a name tie. Save refuses to write through symlinks (v2.1.216+). The approval prompt offers 'Yes, and don't ask again for <name> in <path>'. Saved workflows take an `args` global, and /reload-skills picks up edits. The meta block must be a pure literal, or /<name> drops out of autocomplete. Source: workflows.md 'Save the workflow for reuse', 'Pass input to a saved workflow', 'Edit a saved script'.

Plugin-distributed workflows: a workflows/ directory at the plugin root, or the `workflows` manifest field. They are namespaced /<plugin>:<meta.name>. Source: workflows.md 'Distribute a workflow in a plugin'.

Bundled /deep-research workflow (needs WebSearch; reports claims it could not verify as unverified, not refuted) and the bundled /workflow-authoring skill (v2.1.248+). Source: workflows.md 'Bundled workflows', 'Edit a saved script'.

Size-guideline levels and defaults: unrestricted, small <5, medium <10, large <50. The default is medium, or small on Pro with v2.1.271+ (2.1.271 lowered medium from 15). Settable via the workflowSizeGuideline key (v2.1.219+) or /config. A guideline you pick yourself also resets the Large-workflow agent threshold. Source: workflows.md 'Set a size guideline'; settings-reference.md; changelog 2.1.271.

Configurable concurrency: CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS takes 1-256 (v2.1.269). The default of 16 drops when fewer CPUs are available. Source: workflows.md 'Behavior and limits'; env-vars.md.

Prompt-cache sharing in a fan-out: agents with the same model, effort, agent type, tools, schema and working directory share a cached prefix. Claude Code holds matching siblings for up to CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_PREFIX_STAGGER_MS (default 5000, v2.1.229+) until the first agent's response starts. Workflow agents' cache TTL defaults to 5 minutes even on a subscription; subagentPromptCacheTtl or CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL can set 1h. Source: workflows.md 'Prompt caching in a fan-out'; env-vars.md; settings-reference.md.

Determinism guard for replay: Date.now(), Math.random() and argument-less new Date() throw inside scripts, and import() fails before the run starts. Scripts get no filesystem or shell access; only agents have that. Source: workflows.md 'Edit a saved script', 'Behavior and limits'.

Run control in /workflows: p pause/resume, r restart one agent, x stop an agent or the run, f filter by status. Stopping one agent with x counts as a failure for replay. Pressing x again re-signals agent processes that are still alive. A relaunch is refused while the stopped run's agents are still alive. Source: workflows.md 'Watch the run', 'Manage runs', 'Resume after a pause'.

Permission gating of the launch: Workflow or Workflow(<name>) allow rules. Auto mode asks only on the first launch and records consent in user settings (skipped when ultracode is on). Manual mode asks every run. -p and the SDK never prompt and use normal permission evaluation. Desktop shows an approval card with Once/Always/Deny. Source: workflows.md 'Approve the plan before it runs'.

On/off controls: the enableWorkflows key (defaults off on Pro, on elsewhere), disableWorkflows, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS, and the workflowKeywordTriggerEnabled key for the ultracode keyword. An in-progress run keeps going when workflows are disabled. Source: workflows.md 'Turn workflows off'; settings-reference.md.

Model controls: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL sets the default model for workflow agents, and CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1 (v2.1.257) forces one model onto all of them. An availableModels allowlist substitutes a model and /workflows warns. 2.1.283 fixed runs started during a model fallback staying on the fallback model. Source: sub-agents.md; env-vars.md; workflows.md 'Cost'; changelog 2.1.283.

-p background wait ceiling: `claude -p` waits for background workflows until 10 minutes of continuous idle (CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS, 0 means no limit), then stops them and drops their partial results. Source: headless.md 'Background tasks at exit'; env-vars.md.

Background-session handoff: workflows survive a background session's process being stopped, restarted or updated (v2.1.196; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BG_EXIT_HANDOFF=1 turns this off). Moving a session to the background replays the run and restarts its running subagents from scratch, and the 'Background this session?' dialog shows how many. Source: agent-view.md; env-vars.md.

Cloud sessions: workflow results are saved with the cloud session's conversation history and survive VM reclamation. The SDK's WorkflowOutput has a 'remote_launched' status for runs sent to a cloud session, with sessionUrl as the resume handle. Source: workflows.md 'Resume after a pause'; agent-sdk/typescript.md WorkflowOutput.

Agent SDK Workflow tool (Agent SDK v0.3.149+). Inputs: script, name, scriptPath, args, resumeFromRunId (same session only). Outputs: runId, taskId, transcriptDir, scriptPath and warning, plus an `error` field set when the syntax check fails even though the status reads async_launched. Source: agent-sdk/typescript.md 'Workflow'.

Hook integration: hooks fire inside subagents with agent_id and agent_type in their input. Stop-hook input includes background_tasks, whose entries have type 'workflow' and the workflow's name, so a hook can tell a session that is finished from one waiting on a workflow. Source: hooks.md common input fields and 'Stop input'.

What ultracode changes beyond the old doc: it lifts the session's 20-subagent concurrent limit (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS, v2.1.217+), skips the auto-mode first-launch approval, and suppresses the Large-workflow warning. No setting turns ultracode off by itself; an effort cap below xhigh does. Source: workflows.md 'Let Claude decide with ultracode'; sub-agents.md 'Concurrent subagent limit'.

Usage visibility: the /usage breakdown attributes recent usage to subagents, which covers workflow agents, as a share of the total, computed from local session history. Source: costs.md 'Plan usage breakdown'.

Availability: all paid plans, the Anthropic API, Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform and Microsoft Foundry. On Pro the user must turn workflows on in /config. Source: workflows.md top note; settings-reference.md enableWorkflows.
